text: I'm going to review this specific one first, because a majority of people know of Starbucks. So, this one is quit busy before and after work, also for lunch. There are NO couches, so don't come here to lounge. It's also a bit of a weirdo magnet. I was in their one day and this guy came in was waving his hands around in the air pretending he was deaf, but NOT signing anything coherent. They tried to help him and he just stood at the counter, they finally asked him to leave and he wouldn't. Then another guy was standing outside spraying himself and the air with windex, while an overweight white guy enters in African garb and a 1980's portable tape deck. So, come here for the entertainment, come here for a coffee, but don't expect to lounge around like at other Sbux. What makes Starbucks worthwhile? 1. Consistency and 2. Service. I'm not picky about my coffee, so I could really go anywhere as long as it's close. I spent most of my college years (avoiding study time) in a coffee shop before I even heard of Starbucks. But, what i love is that I know with virtual certainty that if I walk into a Starbucks anywhere in the world, i can get the same drink and they will remake it if I don't like it without hesitation. Now, we've had our run-ins with Sbux employees, (Willow Grove, New Hope...I'm looking at you.) But, entering an unknown local place, is hit or miss by a large margin. Did the guy order enough milk for the day? Are they using a crappy mix? Do they even want you there? You never know, but when you find the place you like it's yours forever (or until Starbucks moves in down the street.) Starbucks, is definitely expensive. So, don't feel bad about sending your drink back...but don't be a jerk about it. We're all staring at you. TIP: GET A STARBUCKS CARD! FREE: 2 hours of wifi a day, free beverage with bean purchase and free 'select' syrups and milk.

text: In case anyone is wondering, in regards to the last two comments, the Miramar is quite unlikely to open in 2009. It was a great family place, I grew up going to this place, with the trains running through the property, the beach, the charming cottages and the diner. There was a cantankerous elderly Frenchman named Jacques who sat around in a speedo handing out boogie boards to the kids and flirting with the female guests. He got an obituary in the local paper when he passed away, and is a legend in Santa Barbara. I once saw a framed portrait of him in a private home in Rincon, no joke. But yes, the days of an affordable beachfront hotel in Montecito ended in 2000, when Ian Schrager, co-founder of the legendary Studio 54 and hotelier douchebag extraordinaire, closed it and never reopened it, selling it in 2004 to Beanie Baby founder and billionaire Ty Warner. Schrager bought the place for 31.5 million and sold it to Warner for 45 million. I don't know how much Schrager spent on the place in the interim, but one look at the place will tell you he still made a nice profit on the deal. Schrager is widely hated in Montecito for this, I might add. People in Montecito don't like eyesores, and the chainlink fences and abandoned bungalows of the Miramar, in one of the most prominent spots in town, isn't pretty. The place is still, almost 8 years after closing, still empty, and it will be at least 10 years before it opens again. And it's not just the eyesore factor - it's the fact he ruined one of the best places in Santa Barbara. Ty Warner, who owns most of Montecito already, dumped the hotel in January 07 - he didn't do much to it either. It then passed to Rick Caruso, a big shot LA developer who's responsible for some god-awful shopping complexes down there like The Grove. Caruso also has his eye on the LA mayoral office. For now, though, he is currently trying to turn it into a hotel with retail shops and god knows what else, but he's running into all kinds of shit that happens when you try to build stuff on the beach in California. He's currently (as of June 23, 2008) fighting an EIR, and threatening to abandon the project if the inconvenient and annoying environmentalists don't just leave him alone and let him build whatever he wants, no questions asked. That won't happen, so, long, long, long story short, don't expect the Miramar to reopen anytime soon.

text: If I could, I'd give this place negative stars. To start with, the Starlight is in an industrial wasteland that is reminiscent of scenes from "Escape from New York". All I needed was Ernest Borgnine to pull up and it would have been complete. The venue is a cross between a roller rink and a VFW hall, with the bar in the back and the main floor up front. One of the main things that screws up this venue, besides the crappy sound people, are SIX, count them, six columns that run through the main floor of the venue. So basically you have to get right up front or get to the sides in order to see anything. My friends and I were lucky enough to get a booth on the side so we had seating. Although we had three people decide that it was ok for them to sit on our table once the show started. The geniuses didn't even check to see if the table was bolted down, so SURPRISE the whole table tilted up and they fell down along with my drink. The show I saw was an under 21 show, so of course they made everyone entering the bar area show ID. They banded the OVER 21 people. Then I had to stand in line while one of two servers for 500+ people made drinks. while getting elbowed by non-armband wearing people. Just lovely. To top it off, beer prices were outrageous. 5 bucks for a decent bottle of beer that we had to of course consume only in the bar. The show I saw had an amazing band and lead performer. However the music was greatly diminished due to several factors. First and foremost was the lack of balancing of each band members instruments. The sound people failed to recognize that both the keyboard and guitarists sound levels were much higher than the lead vocalists. So logically, one would either turn their instruments down, or turn up the lead vocalists during softer songs. Right? Well obviously the sound guys slept through that class since they didn't key into it almost the entire show. I also had problems with people snapping multiple flash pictures during the show. Hello? Anyone? Make an announcement before the show "No pictures during the show". Plenty of other venues do it. Lastly, and this is probably a futile comment, but its a music show. You paid over 20 bucks to listen and see a band. Why not actually LISTEN to it instead of talk and let the band be your backround music? Oh yeah, and the bathrooms stunk of urine after they finally let us in around 7:40pm. Not to mention they had signs up in the women's room that said "Please do not flush toilet paper down the toilet". Real sanitary guys. I hope this isn't typical of Philly shows. Otherwise I may never see another show here.

text: Of all of the noodle houses I frequent, including the ones in Chinatown, this location of Hoang Long is one of my favourite Vietnamese restaurants. I don't often come to West Edmonton Mall exclusively for the purpose of dining, but I do occasionally just to come here. This is a small but well laid out, bright restaurant in the Chinatown area of the Mall. It serves different kinds of pho noodle soups, as well as rich or noodle dishes with chicken, beef, or pork. The bowls of pho are enormous - probably the biggest I have ever had without ordering a large size. And it tastes great. I also really like anything with lemongrass grilled chicken or beef. As an appetizer, I order skewers of the chicken and beef, which are long and loaded with meat and covered in a spicy peanut sauce. They take a while to prepare but are worth the wait. To drink I often order tea, iced coffee over condensed milk, or a "sunrise" - a combination of orange juice, pineapple juice, and grenadine, served in a tall glass. The drink is as great to look at as it is to drink. A family owned establishment with other Edmonton locations, Hoang Long has great food, good prices (slightly higher than other Vietnamese restaurants by a dollar or two for most dishes), and good service.

text: Let me first apologize to my mother for the hurt I'm about to cause her. Now. This is hands down the best fried chicken in St. Louis. Being originally from the south I don't make that statement lightly. Crisp, thin, crunchy crust that is muy flavorful covering moist and tender chicken. The best part? It's that way each and every time. No inconsistencies here. Personally, we buy a box (yeah, I said a box) of plump drumsticks to bring home for guests and a handful of their homemade hot sauce. But if you're into white meat it's all good. By the way, it's also phenomenal cold and doesn't get soggy so for that next picnic outing you could do a hell of a lot worse. Chicken isn't the only thing they are rocking out, but it's hard to order anything else. The catfish is also ridiculous, and these little corn fritters they make are extremely addictive. Lots of other options, but chicken is king here. There are a few booths and tables inside if you desire to eat in. While there's certainly nothing special about the decor, it's always been very clean on my dozens of visits. The people who know about Porters, are religious about Porters. And to be honest I'm a bit hesitant to write this review since it's already busy enough and I don't particularly want to wait in line. It's easy to pass by this place and never notice it, it's just North of a KFC (which I find hilarious that the people going to that KFC don't know what is 100 yards away) and on the same side of the road. p.s. - They do make a "spicy" version of their chicken, but I'd advise against it since it's a different crust altogether (cornmeal based). And while very good, it really doesn't compare. So just get regular, slap some hot sauce on that bitch. Who needs Calgon to take you away when there's Porters?

People have mentioned that it's homemade at Carl's, but I think it's actually Dad's or A&W. I know it's some regularly distributed brand, though. The fries were completely unremarkable (neither of us can even remember what they were like; not worth the calories). Top that off with indifferent or down right surly service. Admittedly, it was kind of late on a night with crappy weather, but there was certainly no indication that they were happy about having customers. The upside is that the tiny old school diner building is really worth checking out. It's not clean, it's not well kept, but it is authentic. Other than that, I can't recommend this place. Go once to see the building and you've pretty much covered Carl's Drive In. And don't worry if you don't like it. There was something extremely casual about this restaurant. It had the shiny silverware, the while linen, and the first class service, but at the same time the table was covered with butcher paper with drawings of cartoon rabbits and turtles who happily ignore their fate of turning into pot pie and soup, respectively. I found this devilishly hilarious. But that was my last moment of humor, because it was Chef Paul who got the last laugh. The food was ridiculous. Crazy. Out of control. Off the fa-jazzy. It was my first time having fried green tomatoes. It was the most enjoyable "losing-virginity" experience ever. I highly recommend it. But it was the shrimp chipotle remoulade that really put it over the edge. Other tastes of the evening included the turtle soup, bronzed swordfish, panned chicken breast, and Chartres Street jumbalava. Had death followed me on the tails of this meal, I would have embraced my place in the afterlife, happy, full, and content.

The locally sourced cheese were served with a combination of jams, fruits and nuts that were well thought out and delicious. The meat board, which I think is one of the best in the city, and all made in house. Served with a spicy mustard, an olive tapenade, and some cornichons. Yum. Both plates were served with toast and bread slices. The toast rocks. I moved on to the chicken live/foie grois pate. Presented in a small cruet with a few cranberries on top and a small salad of pickled carrots and beets. This is probably the best pate I've had in Philly, and the best I can remember in a long time. It was so good, I ordered two as my friend stared noshing on mine. Delicious. I moved on to the beet salad, which was incredible. perfectly cooked heirloom beets and fantastic greens perched atop a whipped goat cheese, It really doesn't get any better than this. My only mistake was having two orders of pate before this, as this dish can be rich with that goat cheese. so split the pate with a guest and order this - you'll love it. My guest also had the soup, which was filled with chicken, beans, and escarole, and quite delicious, as well as the pasta lunch offering, which was a lovely lemony offering with ricotta. No room for dessert, but we will be back!

text: WINNER: Best Non-Bar Way to Spend a Saturday Night in Tucson Yes, it's an outdoor flea market, replete with dirt aisles, toothless patrons, and digestive-issue-causing junk food. And here's why it's damn fabulous: 1. It's free. 2. There is a golf cart with a keg in the back that makes regular rounds--no need to wait in line at the concession stand for a beer. 3. With a combination of permanent and transient vendors, there are always treasures awaiting you. There's a great combination of handmade crafts, secondhand goods, and cheap crap no one really needs. Some of my finds at the swap meet: *3 pack 150 sheet notebook paper, 50 cents *bright green cardigan sweater, 25 cents *wicker wine picnic set (worth about $80 at Crate and Barrell), 10 cents [Well, I owe a particular thank you to crystal meth for the last one, a desperate plea from a madly pacing, scabby, near-toothless girl who was desperate to score because "it's my birthday."] 4. Best people watching in Tucson, bar none. 5. You can do all of the following within 50 yards: shop for produce, get a spare key made, have jewelry repaired, ride a carousel, pose for your own calendar/t-shirt, or get a tattoo. 6. It manages to be both family and thug friendly. 7. The best doughnuts in Tucson are sold right out of the fryer at a booth in the front. 8. You're on the right side of town to hit the TTT afterwards.
label: POS

text: I read how one person called this place overpriced in their review, and I read how another said, "how can it be overpriced when nothing on the menu is over $10?" Well, now I know. The portion size is TERRIBLE!!! I paid $9 for a mini pizza. It was mini alright. I could have gotten 3 or 4 slices at Lorenzo's, and it would have been tastier, not to mention WAY more food! My bf got the Belgian dip sandwich. It was very tasty, but just a sandwich...no sides or anything, and for $10..screw that. We got the "featured cheese fondue" instead of the cheddar b/c I read how everyone hated the cheddar on yelp. I told the waiter about this, and he agreed that the cheddar fondue was terrible. Well, the featured fondue that he promised was much better was brown. Yes, brown. At first I thought he accidentally brought us chocolate. We also tried 2 cheeses, which were okay. Ah yes, and all of the bread that came with everything was NOT fresh by any means. Also, there was 1 guy running the whole shebang. He had a full bar and 3 tables. Besides him, there was a cook and that's it. I stopped by here to pick up a gift card last month and it took FOREVER. I was ignored for a long time. The bartender was too busy flirting w some guys at the bar. I asked for a $50 gift cert and she was like well, I have one for $250. I was like HUH?? Uhh NO! Then she was like well, I have one $25 gift cert left. Ok, great. They need more staff that are not teenage hipsters. However, I did try a very strong, very good glass of wine. The beer prices were average I guess, but let's just say next time I wanna drink wine or have dinner, it won't be here.

text: I used to be a CarShare member for about a year - until they started screwing things up royally! #1 - Charging for estimated mileage. Just because I rent a car for over 24 hours, doesn't mean I'm actually going to go over the mileage limit! How can they just ASSUME these things? Very unfair.. And after they charge you for the milage that you NEVER drove, it's a pain in the butt to have to call them to get your money refunded. #2 - Gas cards being taken out of the cars..Which means you have to pay out of pocket for gas! Isn't the whole purpose of opting for this program to save money and NOT have to pay for gas? Why don't they issue personal gas cards to all of their members, that pull from the same gas account? #3 - Smarmy e-mails telling me that it's not recommended to rent a car for weekend trips, and that it's not really "car sharing"..and now I have to pay more. I was here after an after party, around 5 AM. (It's always fun to observe fellow patrons, wondering what party they came from, who else is hungover, or what job they're starting/ending for the day.) Early morning food has a way of rousing one from a drunken stupor for a bit. I had two eggs (any style), with potatoes, toast, and Canadian bacon for about $6. My breakfast was deliciously filling and deliciously greasy - and didn't break the bank. Service was friendly, quick, and sympathetic - a few friends were out of commission, and luckily our waitress was patient, took our orders in stride, and brought everything right out.

text: By now everyone knows this bar is associated with the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia show and a lot of these reviews mention that. So to warn you, I have no affiliation with the It's Always Sunny show, nor do i have crushes on any of the actors or actresses in the show, or the owners of this bar. I watched the show few times and thought it was funny. Also, I used to go to Skinners and whatever it was called before that, and this has always been a prime people watching outdoor drinking spot in OC, so we decided to come here for drinks and dinner. The difference as of at least yesterday, now that Mac's is here, is that the service at the outdoor tables was great. The waitress didn't leave us hanging for our next beer or check just because we were outside. On top of that, there are more than 10 beers on tap AND the food was really good. I had the Seitan Sandwich which was actually the size of two sandwiches and amazing (the shoestring fries it came with weren't great, though). The app special was mexican style corn on the cob, with chipotle and parm, again - amazing for bar corn (could have come with corn holders, though, it was messy). My husband went for one of the "gravy fry" entrees - basically thick cut fries with steak and veggies and cheese on top. Juju Ginger beer and Carlsberg on tap. I was only inside for 5 seconds so I dont know if the old divey bathrooms were redone, but I would definitely go back to find out. The one thing (has to be something) is that the menus we got handed to us were absolutely gross. Ratty tattered greased up thin paper. The menu deserves better that that and so do I. Eew!
label: POS

text: I want to like Pastiche, really I do. The owners do lots of good things for local charities and the menu is intriguing and only moderately expensive. But more often than not this restaurant fails to execute. I've eaten here on a number of occasions and about half the time it's satisfactory and the rest of the times it flirts dangerously with disaster. The service is lackadaisical to the point of being catatonic. On the most recent visit it took 25 minutes to get an espresso, and this was at a time when there were only a handful of tables that were occupied. On another visit we waited a half hour to get a bottle of wine and one scotch and soda from the bar. On yet another occasion the waiter promised to bring bread right out and then he'd take our orders (we'd already been waiting about 15 minutes, but at least we had drinks that time) and then he disappeared for another 20 minutes. On yet another visit only three of our four orders came out to the table, and by the time the fourth plate arrived, the rest of us had finished. Don't even try to eat here if you happen to be on a schedule -- you'll never make it out on time. The good news is that by and large the food is quite good once it finally gets to your table. The only mishap with food I've experienced was when a burger came out accompanied by stone-cold onion rings. Yuck.

text: Food: Expensive and not that great. The Italian beef sandwich was small and the au jus was too salty. The sandwich was $10 and came with a small dish of cole slaw. Not worth it. The chili cheese fries were also disappointing. There wasn't enough cheese on it and the chili was mediocre. The special they had that day was a pulled pork sandwich (with sweet potato fries) for $6.95 and it was really good. I think that was the best thing I had there. My friend said that it was too sweet though. Drinks: Root Beer Float was expensive, didn't have enough ice cream in it, and was not that great. It may be because the root beer isn't that good. Carl's Drive In's is better. The chocolate malt I got was too sweet and liquidy. Even with my limited experience with malts, I'm pretty sure that malts are supposed to be thick. Mine was the consistency of a melted shake. To demonstrate my point: I couldn't finish all of it and brought the rest back home and put it in the fridge. When I took it out to drink 7 hours later, it was exactly the same as it was in the restaurant...liquidy. Service was good and the staff was very friendly. However, my partner in crime and I like refills on water and we never got any even after sitting with our cups empty for about half of the meal. No, I do not believe I will ever go back again. The drinks, which they supposedly specialize in, are mediocre to terrible and the food is not good. I give it two stars because of the friendly atmosphere.

text: In my opinion, one of the best pizza joints in town. The wine and pizza bar is a great concept and it is in the heart of what is now being referred to as "Restaurant Row." I had been there a couple times for drinks and although the wine list is small, there is a nice variety. We started with the grilled zucchini, which had a smoky romesco sauce and shaved pecorino cheese. The smokiness was a little too much for me, but my boyfriend liked it. We opted for the Sopressata pizza, after a recommendation from the table next to us. I am glad we took their advice. The kalamata olives were a nice compliment to the sopressata and the crust is just perfect. Not too thick, with just the right doughy-ness. There wasn't any grease on the pizza, which I recently learned is due to low quality ingredients (and P.S., patting the grease with a napkin does save calories), so you know you are getting good stuff. At the end of our meal we were already planning what we wanted to try next time.

text: I am afraid it looks like there is a drop in quality - both on the ingredients and execution front, resulting in an unappealing quality to price quotient. When most entrees are in the $28-$34 range, which is towards the high end for Pville and the competition surrounding you is offering much more innovative and better executed food at a more reasonable price point, it is time to wake up and smell the coffee. The $12 mussels appetizer had exactly 6 molluscs. The "exotic" mushroom salad had cold mushrooms found in most supermarkets and was drowning in dressing. The $28 diver scallops had nice sized scallops, but seemed like they were seared ahead of time and were sitting out as they were not warm and almost soggy (could have happened if the scallops were placed under a tap). The medium Angus burger was obliterated until it was gray through and through. The fresh fries offered a glimmer of hope once the excess salt was wiped off. In retrospect we should have demanded more and sent some of the dishes back, but we were hungry so we chowed on. Dessert was some coffee and a tummy ache.

I don't have any plans returning unless it is an event (wedding or celebration). Won't be by choice.

text: I've been here twice and both times I have had a good time! The first time was on a weekend night and it was unbelievably packed. But somehow it was still easy to order drinks from the bar. And can I just say I am in love with their $4 special. A can of Tecate and a shot of tequila. Brilliant. The music is good and the crowd always seems to be having a great time. The bartenders are friendly and easy to grab their attention. This place just has a good/fun atmosphere. The second time I went here I decided to sit down and get dinner. It was on a saturday night and was packed so we sat at the bar and had a drink till a table came available. It was maybe a 30 minute wait which wasnt too bad. The chips and salsa are excellent and they give you a good amount. I had the spcial which was 3 enchiladas. I had cheese enchiladas and they were excellent. The portion was huge and you get a lot of beans and rice as well. Prices ae good here and the waiters were friendly also. I definitely need to come back and try their margaritas and get a pitcher of something to drink. I am not sure about parking since we cabbed it there, and I am told there is an outdoor patio during warm weather so im excited to check that out. For this being my first Mexican restaurant in Philly, I am pleasantly surprised!!! And like I mentioned, Tecate and a shot of tequila for $4. Awesome!

text: We arrived at Amada with great anticipation. We were told by everyone we meet here that it is the best restaurant in Philly. We have had such good food in Philly that we were excited to experience the latest rave in town. We were underwhelmed! The service was great, friendly, professional, but the food did not stand up to its reputation. Maybe its because we have these styles of restaurants in LA and the locals have found a new way of serving Prosciutto but the much talked about salad -Ensalada de Jamon - Serrano Ham and fig salad was disappointing, the fig was not fresh fig but dried and the selection of the Serrano Ham could have been better. The clams and sausage was a great Spanish traditional with little flavor. We could have been eating tofu! We didnt get this restaurant. The artichokes were good, Barrimundo was ok. I really think that the locals are enjoying the Spanish Tapa craze that has swept the country a while ago. But I have had much better Tapas in LA and New York. I would rather eat at other restaurants in this city of fine restaurants. So my advise, if you are coming in from out of town, skip this one and try other great seafood establishments in the City.

text: I stayed here the first time several years ago during Voodoo Fest when a friend got it when he used priceline or hotwire. I enjoyed my stay that time as well. So when we were booking our current trip for 9/16 to 9/20 and our original option of staying in a house in Marigny didn't work out we decided to wait and priceline a week or so before our trip. I had a feeling we'd get this place when I was putting the bid in. I had gotten an email for a 4 star in the CBD at $55 a night pop up so I went for it. We had 3 couples going and I booked 3 rooms for 4 nights. Came out to $268/room after the fees. We were very pleased with our stay and the staff was very nice minus the lady who worked in the little shop downstairs. We went in to ask if she could make change for the streetcar and asked her a question about it. She actually ignored us at firs when were standing in front of her trying to talk to her. But the actual front desk staff and all the staff we saw on our floor, in the elevator, etc were pleasant and chatty. We were able to check in at about 12:30 pm when we got there from the airport on that Thurs. They only had 1 King bed available which my bf and I took and had planned to wait until they had one but the other 2 couples didn't care. One of them actually ended up with a room with a balcony. We were all on the 10th floor. Our bed was comfy and the room was nice and cool. I actually probably was keeping it too cold but if felt nice considering it was nice and muggy outside so loved it when we'd get to our rooms. haha I do think the 2 queen beds are actually 2 double beds or so say our friends. But again we had a king which was great. The water pressure in the shower is a little hard but mostly because could have been fixed with a better showerhead. We didn't use the mini bar/fridge at all. But I think I opened it at one point it was a bit on the warm side. But didn't make a difference for us. The location is a few blocks the other side of Canal from the quarter but a nice break from the noise and hustle & bustle. And the St Charles Street car has a stop right across the street and less than half a block. There are several restaurants in walking distance and CVS & walgreens. Always lots of cabs out front. We chose not to have housekeeping the first 3 days and left our sign up on the door. 4th day we took it down but seemed to have been skipped over. text: This review is from the perspective of a reptile owner. Keep that in mind. I really wanted to like this place. I tried it over and over and over again for food (mealworms) for my lizard. But unless it is Tuesday--the shipment day, it just became too common that I would head there and they would be out of mealworms. Also, it wasn't uncommon for many dead mealworms to be in the containers they would sell. Once I caught on to this, I would check before leaving the store, and they always would throw some more in there, but still... . I guess they do have some sort of cricket-purchasing club, so if interested, it's likely worth asking about that. They never--never--had the lights I liked in stock, which seemed odd since it was a fairly standard light for a fairly standard pet (bearded dragon). They do seem to be very well stocked for fish and fish tanks. They also have a decent selection of toys and equipment for dogs and cats. Birds and bird supplies are also stocked. As for the selling of dogs and cats--they have a selection, in cages. I'm very biased on this, and fully aware of the hypocrisy since I bought a captive bred lizard. But to me, I'll always get my dog(s) from the Humane Society or pound. I wish people would adopt those in need instead of supporting the trade and distribution of dogs (I hesitate to say puppy mills, but I guess I just did it. Rant over). The staff is certainly courteous though. I give them that. And there are special "pet-related" events held occasionally as well.

They didn't serve, they simply walked around. Not once did they offer to order drinks for us and I repeat, we waited over an hour and 20 minutes. After half an hour of waiting, the blond wife's mantra was "5 more minutes, a table is leaving soon". I have read reviews and heard from neighbors that the food is spotty -- some things are good, some not. The mussels get good reviews, for example. However, the service was horrible, and the owner and his entourage walking around but being completely useless turned what could have been a nice evening there, into one where we ultimately walked out hungry, thristy, and disgruntled. The good news is that we went to a competing establishment where we thought the food would be worse but it turned out to be great! I'll be writing a review for that separately. Summary: Nice ambience but HORRENDOUS service, and a complete and utter inability to turn tables means get here early or not at all.

text: My husband and I have been customers of Philadelphia Scooters for a long time. He purchased his first scooter from them and has purchased two other scooters since. Initially, working with Philadelphia Scooters was great, and my husband referred four other customers to them. However, our last experience with Philadelphia Scooters was so bad that we would never refer anyone to them or buy a scooter there again. Less than four months after buying a 2008 Genuine Stella, we began to have serious issues, particularly with the engine stalling out. We took the scooter back to the shop and were refused service. First, we were told that our warranty was invalid because the scooter was slightly over 500 miles and we hadn't brought it in for its scheduled maintenance. While I agree that we had technically violated the warranty, one would think that a small local business with a pretty selective customer base -- and one that had sold a total of seven scooters through our patronage and references -- would overlook a minor technicality, especially when other shops in the city do. Philadelphia Scooters was not only firm about this but also rude and condescending. Then, after we agreed to pay the full cost of repairs, we were told that they did not have the parts we needed (which at this point, not knowing what the real problem was, were pretty basic parts) and that they weren't going to order them for us. Basically, they didn't want to work on the scooter period. My guess is that, because they get so much maintenance and repair business (hence the weeks to month long wait times), they feel that they can pick and choose what they'd like to do, based on what's convenient for them? However, to us it was pretty surprising considering that we bought the scooter from them and they're the only Genuine dealer in Philadelphia. After being sent on our way, we went to another Philadelphia scooter dealer, who managed to figure out the problem (faulty air valve), cut us a few deals after hearing about the raw one we got from Philadelphia Scooters, and helped us get in touch with Genuine about the bad scooter we'd been sold. Throughout this process, Philadelphia Scooters remained unresponsive when we needed their assistance and pretty much shut us out about the fact that, regardless of our warranty invalidation, the scooter was bad when they sold it to us. We will never go to or refer anyone to Philadelphia Scooters again. Not only were we treated unfairly, but we also found that the staff was rude, condescending, unhelpful and unresponsive as soon as there was a problem. This was ultimately a situation that was not their fault but Genuine's; however, the treatment we received there means that they will be the ones to lose our business.

text: Langhorne needed a place like Miller's Ale House. They're always open late and their kitchen closes at 1:30am! Once you're there however you'll be pleasantly surprised with tons of seating, TVs, and drinks. As the name states this is an ale house so don't expect restaurant-style atmosphere (read: do not bring your kids here). Do expect a GREAT place to come in and watch the game while having a few drinks with your friends. My friends and I went over on opening night so I was a bit hesitant to try any of the food that might be difficult to cook. I figured new cooks might mean they're still not used to the menu items. But the bartender told me that the staff is quite good and to order anything. So I went for the Fish Tacos. They were awesome. They had a great spicy kick to them and arrived pretty quickly for it being so crowded. I was told next time to try the Zingers as an appetizer so I'll be sure to order them next time. There aren't many places in the Langhorne area with a good beer selection. Hulmeville Inn and Isaac Newtons are the only ones I know of in the area that are worth visiting for the beer. Well you can add Miller's Ale House to the list! They have 35 taps and bottled beers too. They have tons of your usuals but they also have a good selection of local breweries and they do a great job on keeping seasonals on tap. They also have some really great deals on beer, $2.95 Leinenkugels all day! I think the only "full price" beer I had was a Hooegarden. They also had a really cheap deal on pitchers of Miller Lite ($5) or $2 bottles all day. If I still lived in the Levittown area this would be my new local sports bar. I'm out in Jamison now but when I'm back in the area I'll definitely be stopping into Miller's Ale House.

text: This was my third half marathon, second Rock n Roll event. I've been to countless other marathons to support family members this was by FAR the worst experience I've ever had at a race. The Good: The good was great, which is why I am giving the race two stars. The course was nice, a bit hilly for this flat lander, but I was up to the challenge. The spectators were FANTASTIC. The music on the course was nice and professional sounding and even though I'm not a country music lover, I enjoyed it. The nutrition and hydration support during and food after were good. The medal was nice and good quality. The rain and tornado warnings were handled as well as could be expected, it was a disappointment not getting to hang out at LP field afterward, but I think the lack of after party was a good move on the race director's part. Tornado warning and lighting strikes aren't worth it. The bad: The bad, was horrible. My great complaint with this race was the complete lack of either skills or motivation by Nashville PD to direct people or move traffic. We sat beginning at 5am 3 miles from LP stadium on the interstate. We did this for 2 hours. When we finally arrived on Shelby there were police officers standing in the middle of the intersections looking pretty, but not much else. They didn't direct traffic and certainly did nothing to alleviate the gridlock. There was no parking at LP field when we got there. When we finally found parking, we had to run 3 miles to the start because we had no access to shuttles. We missed the start and took forever to catch up to the race. In my opinion, LP field isn't appropriate to park that many people (which is hard to believe since it seats 70k and the race was less than 30k) and the Nashville Metro PD are ill equipped or don't care to actually DIRECT traffic. Another reviewer gave the pre-race parking/traffic control a grade of "F"", I cannot in good conscience give it a grade that high. Getting out of town after the race was also horrific but that could be attributed to the horrible weather so I'll give the PD a pass on that. The things I wrote above were hard say because overall the people of Nashville are awesome, the food is good, the course was great, and the runners were fun and friendly. I don't want to demean all of the hard work the fabulous volunteers did. If you decide to do this race, leave your hotel at 3:45am (no, I'm not exaggerating), then possibly you'll make it to the start on time and have a non-towed parking space. Or stay at a spendy downtown hotels. Or have a friend drop you off at the start. If you can't do any of those things, stay home or go to another marathon town.

text: As an Asian California native, I've had my fair share of good sushi. Since moving to St. Louis, I've been on the hunt for decent sushi. Being that it is nearly right across from my apartment, Kampai was an easy find. I actually went to Chi Sushi and Drunken Fish before I tested out Kampai so it wasn't that I settled on the first sushi joint within reach. My first time there, I flew solo and sat at the bar, getting to know the sushi chef, Sean (unfortunately, he moved away). He learned of my affection for uni and gave me the lowdown on how they obtain their fish. A week later, I came back and was greeted by name by both the sushi chef and the waitress, Nancy. Both the waitresses - Nancy and Joy are absolute sweethearts (after introducing her to my now long-distance bf who came to visit, Nancy always asks to see how we're both holding up long-distance). Be nice to them! I've brought tons of friends here and they've all enjoyed the attention and service lavished upon them. My bf says you can judge a sushi restaurant by its miso soup. Why? It come standard with every meal and can be very easily slighted by the kitchen. If they care about the quality of their food, they will pay attention to the miso soup. Needless to say, Kampai's soup is fantastic. What I love THE most though, is their salad. I've never encountered another sushi restaurant that used the same sauce (I later found out they make the sauce themselves). It's light and fruity (made from a bunch of different fruits) and is probably my favorite salad dressing. Soup and salad come standard with each meal, don't skip out on it! I come here without fail every single week to get my sushi fix and it's the only place I go for sushi. Size-wise and creativity-wise, the sushi in St Louis simply cannot compare to the elaborate rolls they dream up in California. I've come to accept it, and have let it go. Tips: - If you plan to come here often, save yourself a few bucks in the long run and purchase the Kampai rewards card - a $5 fee will get you 3% back on every bill that you can accumulate to spend later. - The quantity of sashimi in the chirashi is the same for lunch and for dinner. The price is different. - Print out their Happy Hour coupon and get 25% off your entire bill Monday-Thursday 5-6 PM 5 stars for the sense of home they've given me!

text: Definitely the biggest disappointment in New Orleans. Terrible food, even worse service. A friend and I went here for their famed Sunday jazz brunch. Obviously, my friend had finished her appetizer by that point, so we ate separately. Not ideal. For our entrees, I ordered a fritatta with crab, tomatoes and cheese. The crab was so salty I couldn't eat it, the cheese was a gooey melted sauce that was closer to butter than cheese (and was covering the entire plate), and the eggs were undercooked and runny. Even worse, my friend, who is a vegetarian and had told the water so repeatedly, ordered a veggie omelet, took her first bite, and bit into a huge chunk of crab. She's allergic to shellfish -- hence ordering a tomato, fennel and watercress omelet -- so this didn't go well. Again-- profuse apologies, a promise to come right back with a re-cooked dish, and then 10 minutes went by. Since I wasn't eating my entree (the waiter never asked me how it was, incidentally) she would have been eating alone anyway, but for the second course in a row one of us was eating alone. Dessert was fine -- I had the peach shortcake, she had the bread pudding. The shortcake was dry and flavorless, but the peaches were very good. Her bread pudding was a little too sweet and a bit dry, but had good flavor. We left utterly unsatisfied -- particularly since brunch, with a bloody mary, came to SIXTY DOLLARS PER PERSON. Apparently the cheezy guitar music in the background was worth all that money? The food definitely wasn't. And despite screwing up nearly everything, no one offered us a drink, or took anything off the bill. Long story short, by 3:00 PM he still wasn't at our place, and was still on another job, and wasn't sure when he could move us. He didn't sound enthusiastic about moving our stuff into a townhouse with 3 stories either, said something about how his guys were sick or tired or short-handed, and suggested that we move our stuff the next day instead, since it was getting dark already. GoPro knew of the logistics of our move like it being a 3 story townhouse, if the guys wanted to complain about it, then they shouldn't have taken our deposit or get out of the moving business. We had everything in boxes. EVERYTHING AND waited around on a weekend for movers that kept us waiting all day long. We had NO IDEA that they would even show up actually. That's how little faith we had in this company. What a waste of time. This was not going to fly. So I called GoPro headquarters to talk to Sean - except nobody picked up the phone at GoPro headquarters on Sunday afternoon. NOBODY WAS THERE. The only guy I could talk to was August. I told him to not bother coming over to our apartment, we were going to find somebody else to move us. We ended up calling Handle With Care Moving and talked to Mike, the owner. Handle With Care moved us within 24 hours and Mike himself personally was on the move and part of the 3-man crew. What a difference when the owner is there on site, and they came in $150 BELOW the estimate GoPro gave us. In the end, it worked out for us because we saved money by NOT going with GoPro and for that we'll give GoPro one star. If we could, we'd give them zero stars. I have no idea why GoPro has so many positive reviews. I think you'd be playing roulette going with GoPro. You won't know if they screwed up your move or if you're getting a crappy move team who complain and will bang up your furniture

text: Yes, there will be a line. Yes, you'll sit at mix-and-match tables. And yes, you'll have to deal with the vagaries of a parking lot shared with a Rite Aid. But the lines move quickly, the seating is comfortable, and parking is always a problem in Drexel Hill, so why should your visit to Ming's be any different? There's no better place for breakfast, anywhere. Ming's pancakes are remarkable -- moist, buttery, and flavorful beyond imagining. Ming uses only the freshest of ingredients and keeps a watchful eye over her small but prodigious galley-style kitchen (which runs like clockwork) and table servers who are young, but skilled. Everyone works together to keep things moving. Ming's coffee is the best French Roast I've ever tasted -- and I'm not a fan of dark roasted coffees, especially in the morning. It's hard to know if all of her coffees are the product of a hand-press, but that's how every cup tastes. Never had a single cup delivered to our table which tasted stale, overbrewed or bitter. My wife loves Ming's teas, which are prepared to perfection. So, take a ride to Drexel Hill and enjoy breakfast at Ming's. You'll be delighted.

Sometimes a local artist will display her work on the walls for you to buy or just enjoy viewing. Kids under 12 get a meat and two, or four veggies for just $4.
label: POS

text: On my recent trip to Reno we visited The Imperial during the Wine Walk. The interior was very spacious and comfortable... booths and tables EVERYWHERE that seemed very private. The beer selection was extraordinary. On the back wall was a HUGE blackboard with all the beers listed. I counted 55 ranging from Pabst blue ribbon at $2 and various others I had never heard of at $13. We ordered a pizza with artichokes, garlic, spinach and red peppers and Asian chicken wings. The pizza was a wonderful lunch choice; light yet satisfying. The Asian chicken wings were amazing. Sweet and spicy with no mistaking the Asian flavor.
label: POS

text: If I am ever in the mood for ice cream, Maggie Moo's is my first choice (in the suburbs)! I have had too many kinds to list, but will name a few. Red Velvet cake with a twinkie add in was so rich that I did not think I would ever be able to finish it. I was wrong! Chocolate ice cream with cookie dough, nothing fancy, but so yummy! I've also had the ice cream cup cakes form the freezer. They were good, but the fresh stuff is waaaayyyy better! I've had the soft serve with a variety of add ins as well. No complaints! The customer service is always excellent. One time really stands out for me. I called at 8:30am and they were closed, but someone answered. I explained that I needed 8 cupcakes and she said she would let me in before they opened. The fact that she answered the phone and it was not regular business hours was impressive. Her stopping her regular routine of making the ice cream and letting me in to buy the ice cream cupcakes was above and beyond.
label: POS

text: This place sucks, as Erin put it so perfectly. I tried not to spend too much time in here, so I didn't check out how everything was arranged. There was lots and lots of dust on the bottle of wine that I got. I came in specifically looking for that wine, so it might have more to say about me than it does the store. The worst part was the staff. I had brought my purchases up to the counter and I had to wait another minute while the two employees finished their conversation before the woman at the register would even begin ringing me up. I may be getting worked up, but if this woman went any slower, she might have started to go backwards. Not a word was said other than "ID" and the money for the purchases Now, I'm usually one of those people who don't even notice bad things because I can make do with just about anything, but this was one of the worst experiences I've had as a customer. It was worse than that time when I was a kid and got accused of stealing from 7-11 (which is hilarious if you know me)...Honestly. The store up on 46th and Lancaster was much better. They don't have many wines, but everyone was much friendlier. Just don't get it mixed up with the one on 51st & Lancaster, that one is even worse than this one.
label: NEG

text: Commercialization is everywhere in this area of South Jersey, but it's almost necessary to talk up the recent Centerton Square businesses and particularly Starbucks. Three words: Twenty-four. hour. caffeine. 24-hour caffeine served in a comfortable setting (although all Starbucks could use more counches/comfy chairs) with the New York Times at your finger tips and muffins and cookies of all sorts. Granted it's pretty cold inside for whatever reason and it IS Starbucks (hence 4 stars instead of 5) but it's nice to have around. And, in attempts to mutate into something with a more personal appeal perhaps, this Starbucks hosted a night of local musical performances the evening before Thanksgiving. Doubtful that Corporate came up with the idea, but they agreed to it! Kudos for that at least, as perverse as it seems.
label: POS

text: Simply put, this may be the best fried chicken to be had in New Orleans. The red beans and rice were on par with the best I had during my stay in NOLA. Service was efficient and courteous. Needless to say, this is not fancy place but it is not to be missed.

text: One of my few enjoyable moments when I was in Tucson. It was a nice breakfast that very nearly felt like a picnic in the vine-covered open air patio. I believe that I left my jacket on as I was not in the sun that morning, but it was really nice to be among nature while eating. There is a gift shop with novelty things and snarky fridge magnets and such, but it's not a big deal. What the hell, yelpers. If you don't want to buy anything, don't buy anything. Get over your hipster asses. It is a cute place. I believe that I bought a magnet as a souvenir that said something funny about being an alcoholic.
label: POS

text: In a nutshell, I've had better. In an area with a bunch of coffee shops, there's very little that makes JJ stand out from the rest of the crowd. While I'm not a fan of the brewed coffee, I will say the espresso-based drinks are well made. The staff seems very friendly and well-trained for the most part, but also seem to get easily overwhelmed if there are more than 2 people in line. The baked goods are outstanding, if a little overpriced. I have to agree with the previous reviewer on the aesthetics. While the overall vibe is kinda cool, it does have a very commercial feel to it, and it gets ridiculously loud in there with every sound seemingly bouncing off the walls. They also just play a "coffee shop" satellite radio station in there with boring acoustic cliche music which can get a little old after a while, although it does provide logical background music since it's easy to ignore. Overall, I miss 3 Beans but JJ isn't terrible.
label: NEG

text: Everything I have ever ordered here has been really well done. But if you are looking for the best item you have to go with the Good Dog Burger. It is stuffed with cheese before cooking and absolutely to die for. I have a friend who demands we eat one every time he is in town. Quizzo once a week. Two floors, better to eat on the second (less bar atmosphere).

text: I just don't understand the hype about Sagami. The sushi was mediocre at best. Their reputation was stellar when I was in college. Fast forward 10 years later, Sagami came up again in conversation and I decided I should definitely give it a go. Sushi is my favorite food, so why not? The appetizers were decent, nothing superb about them. We tried the seaweed salad, miso soup, salad with ginger dressing, and some gyoza. Dinner was mediocre as well - not horrible, but not stellar like I've heard. I had the Sushi B dinner. It was okay, but I've had better quality sushi at Yanagi in Voorhees Town Center, believe it or not. My fiancé had a tuna roll with a yellowtail roll. Again, quality was okay, but nothing to speak of. Overall, not a fan and probably won't be back. I'll give it the benefit of the doubt, for this review, and mark it up as an off-day for Sagami. Still, I don't understand how a restaurant with such a fantastic reputation came off so average. If you like Sagami, you'll LOVE Fuji in Haddonfield or Umi Sushi in Somerdale. These are my two current fave sushi spots. Their food quality, freshness, and atmosphere are leaps and bounds beyond what Sagami offers. Give them a try, instead, if you're in the area.
label: NEG

text: Went to Taco Loco finally after passing in too many times and saying to myself, "I bet that place has awesome tacos". My girlfriend and I went on a Sunday afternoon for some quick hangover curing food. When we got there, only one girl was in line, and she said she had already ordered. After waiting for 15 minutes, we ordered chicken tacos, pork tacos, and a Cuban torta. After another 20 minutes we got our food (so much for being quick). There were a few small bones in the chicken tacos, which tasted almost exactly like the pork tacos (I assumed the bones were in the chicken, but wasn't sure which was which), but the tacos were ok besides that. The Cuban torta was NOTHING like we expected. We excepted some sort of pork, cheese, pickles and mustard. What we got was something with pork, EGG, cheese, pickles, tomatoes and a HOTDOG. WTF? It was a hot mess of a sandwich. With all the other good Mexican options in the vicinity, I will not be stopping back at taco loco.

text: I really like CityTV. I choose this channel to watch my morning news because they have fun with their broadcast. Breakfast television is filmed right here in downtown Edmonton and they really focus on local flavour. They have segments all around Edmonton at schools, gyms, shops etc. CityTV also has pretty good programming as well. They have shows like The Biggest Loser, Parenthood and Cityline. I really like watching local television and this is local television at its best!

text: The ultimate NOLA experience!!! Brunch is a must when visiting. Commander's Palace is without question, one of my favorite restaurants in the country. This is not just eating at a restaurant, but a "dining experience." Dress formally, expect fantastic New Orleans cuisine, and most importantly; take your time and enjoy the atmosphere! It doesn't get any better than this! I started with the Soup Sampler - a combination of turtle soup, duck gumbo, and crab bisque. For my entree, I had the veal, and for dessert, the famous Creole Bread Pudding Souffle. One of the best meals that I've ever had!!! The atmosphere is terrific. A jazz band plays throughout and will eventually make their way to your table for a request. "House of the Rising Sun" was a no brainer for me. At the end of your meal, you will be allowed to walk through the kitchen and observe gourmet cooking at its finest. I cannot stress this enough - take your time and enjoy this amazing restaurant. Plan to spend most of the morning at brunch. Afterwards, take a walk around the beautiful Garden District and enjoy the unique architecture. Look for the painted cornrow fences. *** You can have your car valet parked. However, I circled the block and found plenty of space available on the street. The walk up to Commander's was great!
label: POS

text: I've been to Monk's more often than anywhere else in town. The BF and I have both had memorable dishes here that were fan-tab-ulous. Things I especially love: The beer menus. Because when there are sooo many awesome beers to choose from, it's nice to have something to go by besides just the name. The frites are great but the dipping sauce is out of control. The surprisingly large selection of interesting and satisfying vegetarian food options, including a tasty seitan philly cheesesteak. Some people have mentioned the over-crowdedness, and yes, it can be a problem if you go at certain times (and there's not a lot of room to wait inside). The service has always been very professional and accommodating, never rude. The charming and cozy atmosphere along with the scrumptious foods & beers (oh, and awesome pumpkin cheesecake!) outweigh any minor inconveniences.
label: POS

text: This was our 2nd visit to Terrazza Grill. The decor is warm and inviting. Unfortunately my wife and I are disappointed. First off we were told when we arrived that it would be a 15 - 20 minute wait. It turned out to be 45 minutes. Discovered that they do offer call ahead seating. It is a must to call ahead if you don't want to wait 45 minutes. My wife and I did order a house salad with our entries. I had ordered the raspberry vinaigrette and my wife ordered the creamy Italian. My salad tasted a little odd. I thought they may have used the raspberry vinaigrette sparingly and it was not noticeable. Waiter stopped by the table after I had ate the salad to apologize. He had mixed up the order with another table. The salad I ate had creamy Italian dressing. Oh well it was good. My wife's salad on the other hand had too much cheese and was not enjoyable. On our first trip my wife had the Ribeye Sandwich. She really enjoyed it and was looking forward to having it again. This time the Ribeye had too much fat and the sandwich had too much cheese. On our first visit I had the Salmon BLT sandwich. Not what I had expected but enjoyed it and was determined to try something different. I decided to have their pork tenderloin with creamy parmesan risotto. The pork tenderloin was very good. The creamy parmesan risotto seemed a little heavy on the cream. If you eat here you need to be a fan of creamy sauces. Prices are on the high side. Service was quick. It was pretty loud in the restaurant. The quality of our meals don't justify the cost. Not sure that we will return.
label: NEG

text: It's a little Korean market with a decent selection of dry goods, some frozen items, and a small section of produce. Depending on the time you go, some of the produce can be a little old. It's also wise to check the expiry dates on some goods, as some are past their expiry dates. I usually come to this store mainly to buy the dry goods since it's the closest to where I live. Prices are in the moderate range.
label: NEG

text: I was soured on Geist Family Dentristy when I came here for a regularly scheduled cleaning. During the course of the cleaning, the tech found some spots that she thought were suspiciously soft. She called the dentist in, who examined my mouth and let me know that I had two cavities that needed to be filled. There were two other spots that he checked out, but decided that they were ok and didn't need treatment. Well, I'm pretty freaked out by drills in my mouth, so when I went in to have the work done, I asked for the nitrous. They administer it, and then, while I'm too messed up to protest, the dentist decides that he better go ahead and drill those other two spots after all, so when I come down from the gas, I'm presented with a bill that's twice as high as what I expected to pay. Maybe this is normal, but I don't think so. It seemed shady to me, and I won't be going back here. The only reason I gave it two stars instead of one is because the tech was so pleasant and friendly.
label: NEG

text: Prince Conti had excellent reviews on AARP and was in the heart of the French Quarter, so we booked it. It was not a bad place, probably sufficient when held against other Qtr hotels, but there some things that left me feeling "Meh. I've experienced better." Our room was small, but nicely decorated and clean. It had double beds that were not very comfortable and lacked fitted sheets, so they come undone as you sleep. The kids' bed didn't even have a mattress pad. The bathroom small, but clean. The continental breakfast was woefully uninspired and cheap compared to the fare offered at other hotels on our trip...crossiants that were refrigerated, some fruit. There were no trash cans, you were to put your dirty plates in one of the tubs and paper trash in another. So outside of restocking items as they ran low, no one was staffing it and yet they had a tip jar out. The coffee, however, was excellent. I think the parking was reasonable; it was $25 a day, which was cheaper than what someone else I chatted with in San Antonio paid where he stayed, $36 a day. Quiet, with view of roof and dilapidated buildings next door. You could hear the people behind our beds in the next room, so the walls are thin. I don't remember hearing any noise from above. The beds and the breakfast seriously knock this hotel down in its rating and I think the place is probably more noisy on the weekends (we were in NOLA on a Monday-Tuesday). I'm from Phx where it is HOT and NOLA's summer heat zapped me and seriously effected my ability to enjoy the place. Probably best to visit any other time than Summer.
label: NEG

text: In a word, disappointing. The regular price of this buffet was around $16. And when it was the Reno Hilton's, it would have *almost* been worth it. It would have been worth it back then, when you could take a 2 for 1 deal on Thursdays. As it stands, we took advantage of a "players club" promotion for the price of $7.77 each, for the four of us. Again, it was disappointing. @ $7.77, sure we could have justified it with "you get what you pay for", but I've had better buffets for slightly less, in the area. But, this buffet charges $16, regularly. What do you get for that? Decent service, but hit or miss food. The "tri-tip" was so tough and overcooked it was nearly inedible, the shrimp drab and flavorless, and every variety of rice we tried was hard and crunchy. The black bean soup was extremely over-salted, the pizza crust tasted almost like a frozen food variety's. Most of the other dishes were pretty much just as blah. There were a few decent things though. The BBQ beef ribs were pretty tasty, if not a bit sparse of meat. The pizza, while tasting like the dough was frozen pre-prepared, was ok. The "mexican" chicken & peppers was decent. The guacamole, palatable. The ceasar salad was halfway decent. One thing I did enjoy was the mozarella and tomato salad, but the dressing was way too heavy. The tortellini salad was pretty good, as well as the turkey (if you got small pieces, they didn't seem overcooked like the larger slices) and the mashed potatoes. Desserts were ok, except for the flan. It was pretty bad. The Tres Leches cake was good, as well as the carrot cake, and the other tidbits we tried. Overall score from the four of us, 2 "eh...", 1 "nah..." and 1 "nuh-uh, never again."
label: NEG

text: I tried to hit up every Starr restaurant when I lived in Philly but fell quite short because I was a student and couldn't afford places like Striped Bass. El Vez, though, I made it to twice, and both times were good. On my first visit I came with one friend and we had a reservation (wasn't so lucky the second time). Our waitress was quite nice; we started with the mexican pizza appetizer and I had some kind of enchiladas for my main course. Sorbet sampler for dessert. On the second visit we had to wait a really, really long time, but got one of the neat tables towards the back for larger parties. Our margaritas were good, but a bit overpriced, and I completely forget what I had for dinner. The communal washbasin is neat, too.

The only bright spot was the Zorba (Greek) pizza which was close to being good. Rest all that we ordered (Bruschetta pizza, veg lasagna and veg pasta) was again well below average. It is slightly pricey for the kind of food. Service was good. The food left everyone dissatisfied. Would like to avoid this joint in the future and find a better sports bar or Italian restaurant. text: The 1 star rating is for the convenience of everything being via the internet. Now, the lack of the other rating stars: Like with other banks, you get a debit card, you make charges, you watch your account online to ensure everything works accordingly so that you don't get smacked with a $30 fee for every single charge made in the negative, everything seems peachy. Then after several weeks a bunch of charges don't show up for almost a week, then *poof* -they all show up in 1 morning. Then this happens again a week later. Then -yet again, after another week. Currently, this bank is my only option, within a week I am switching to yet another bank that gouges their customers by withholding charges made so it's 'bank error, in their favor' when overdraft fees appear. Whenever I have called them, they have not been helpful in the least. I usually get something along the lines of "since you can view your account online, there is nothing I can do for you over the phone" or something equivalent. In the hopes of fairly warning future FIBI customers, I'll let my co-workers know about this page so they can post their opinions on this bank as well.

text: Red Lobster may be one of the busiest restaurants in Edmonton. During all seasons and at any time of day the place is packed. During two visits to Red Lobster, my dining companions and myself had to wait ridiculously long time to be seated, and then we had to wait some more for our food to arrive. And the food wasn't all that. Everything on the menu sounds mouthwatering but in reality it is nothing to write home about. On two occasions I have had shrimp linguini Alfredo and rock lobster tail. Neither shrimp nor lobster impressed me. For my linguini Alfredo I was expecting to get large and fresh shrimp that would be the star of the show, but in reality the shrimp were small, overcooked, and rubbery, and smothered in Alfredo sauce the main purpose of which was to cover up the poor quality of the shrimp. Lobster tail, on the other hand, was undercooked. There were raw patches inside, which neither butter nor garlic could disguise. And overall, the food tasted rather bland. If it wasn't for the nice atmosphere in the restaurant, and friendliness of our server, I would have sworn to never come back to Red Lobster. For now, however, I am willing to give it another try. Third time is the charm, they say...
label: NEG

text: The chocolate is absolutely divine, period. The flavors are unique and decadent, and I love exploring the new tastes. Without a doubt, the best chocolate I've ever had. If you don't know what to buy as a present to someone, or if you really owe a favor, this is a great option. It's on the pricey side, but I treat myself to a piece every now and then.

text: Gross, gross, gross! The food was pretty decent. It wasn't anything special in terms of Mexican food; I've definitely had better, but I did like that they offered many combinations of fillings in their burritos, and I could order something off of the menu, rather than having to pick and choose ingredients for a custom burrito. The atmosphere was a bit...creepy. At the time, my friend and I were the only white people in there. Now, that's all fine (lots of Mexicans means decent food, right?), but I could have done without them staring at us the whole time. The T.V. was set to a Spanish station that featured lots of bikini-clad girls dancing around to mariachi music. I'm not sure if this was a positive or a negative. I found it positive because it was like watching the Spanish version of MTV, and I like learning about other cultures. It was also positive because if people were ogling the T.V., they weren't staring at us! So, what knocked Taqueria Rincon Alteno down to one star? THE RESTROOM. IT WAS DISGUSTING. Now, I've been down to Mexico and have dealt with the piss-poor (no pun intended) sewage systems, or even a complete lack of a sewage system. I know that you can't flush the toilet paper down the toilet. In Mexico. However, this is the US of A, and you can't tell me that the sewage system in a ritzy area off the 101 isn't able to handle toilet paper. There is NO reason why I should have to sit next to a basket full of wadded-up, used toilet paper when using the restroom in a place that serves food. That is just gross. I literally felt sick and couldn't finish my food when I came out of the restroom. Don't go to this place, not even for a quick bite to eat and restroom break on a road trip, like I did.
label: NEG

text: I went here years ago with a friend and it's really not changed much. A standard of the central business district and while it draws in a few tourists, it's more a local folks' place. The turtle soup is really good and comes with a dainty pitcher of brandy to pour in for more flavor. You'll also find sandwiches, po' boys, and other casual Creole and southern standards--plus the oysters, of course. The Pearl's been around forever and has a huge neon sign hanging out front over the side walk that looks like it might just fall any moment (not really, but it is a feat of engineering that so grand a sign hangs by so little . . . and for so long!). Another neat aspect of The Pearl is that they've framed pages of several novels that mention the restaurant . . . including Nancy Lemann's seminal "The Lives of the Saints", one of the finest novels ever written about New Orleans. I would suggest The Pearl for oysters or for simple, down-home, New Orleans cooking. Some say it's become more touristy though since I've last been there so I don't know . . . my experience though was fine. :)
label: POS

text: Middle of the week and you're craving barbecue? Happens to me all the time. On a Wednesday night, this place was pretty empty. We were greeted with a warm smile and seated right away. The rib tips are a great way to start the meal. They are tender and flavorful, falling right off the bone. The serving of french fries at the bottom of the basket was laughable, but by the end they were covered in the rib sauce so there's no room to complain. For dinner I ordered the Beef Brisket Sandwich; check the photos. It came out at room temperature, some might argue it was even a little cold. Without sauce the sandwich would have been a little dry, so I tried the Rich & Sassy. For a chain, this restaurant is pretty enjoyable. The only reason I didn't mark 5 out of 5 stars is because I didn't walk over a peanut shell covered floor to get to my table.
label: POS

text: I would first like to point out that there are two Carlucci's in this mall, one is a pizza joint and called Carlucci's Express, the other is a sit down restaurant BYOB and is called Carlucci's Grill. The later is a gem!! Don't fret if you arrive without your vino, there is a Superfresh around the corned in the mall with a liquor store. So get a table, walk down and get a couple of bottles. OK, so now you are served fresh baked italian bread topped with marinara sauce, yum!! The entree choices are many and I have had most (except fish, can't go there). Bar none, they are served piping hot and delicious. Oh and the fresh baked garlic bread, very different, kind of like a whole large pita cooked with olive oil and fresh garlic brushed on top. If you hear singing don't be surprised. They have a few that love to serenade while working, it is very refreshing. All the servers are a little older and have perfected their craft. No teenagers just looking to get it over with here! The ambiance is such that you forget that you are in a strip mall the minute you get inside. The prices are average, you can spend between $10-$20 on an entree. If you have kids with you there is a nice kids menu and crayons to help them color the flip side of the place mat. Turn it in at the end of your meal and they will stamp it with free kids pizza stamp and say, you won!! This makes the day for them, too cool. One of our favorite haunts, definitely worth it!!
label: POS

text: Milagro is a new age Mexican restaurant located in the rear of a newer retail complex in Old Webster Groves. It's a great restaurant with fresh ingredients and food. -Parking-Ample -Decor- Upscale and nice, but monotone. Great metal chandeliers! -Margaritas - Fresh and homemade ($8) -Chips with both sweet and smoky salsas. Yum -Queso fundido -chihuahua cheese w/ poblano rajas and chorizo WOW! We were considering ordering the mole because we heard it was amazing. The owner was kind enough to bring out a sample of the sauce and it did not disappoint. We ordered it, but I wasn't thrilled with the squash medley and rice that accompanied the dish. In addition, the chicken was difficult to eat. It was sauced up and on the bone. So, too messy to eat with hands and too bony to eat with a fork and knife. Still, it was VERY tasty. They ran a special for the night - barbacoa de cordero. HOLY BEJASHUSH!! Juicy, tender lamb seasoned with cumin and other nummy ingredients, served with crunchy Mexican squash and corn cut fresh off of the cob. I hope to see this on the menu again. I highly recommend Milagro. They put a spin on traditional Mexican fare and the restaurant serves fresh homemade food with all fresh ingredients. I for one appreciate fresh ingredients, which are truly hard to come by.

text: This is one of my family's favorite restaurant to go to. We go so often that we don't have to even look at the menu to order ... Carrabba's Gurus! text: Oh Varga Bar... Why won't you just let me love you?!? I mean it. A vintage pin-up theme, truffle mac-and-cheese, outdoor seating, a snooty beer list, an awesome Aussie bartender... there are so many reasons that Varga and I should make beautiful babies together. And those (coupled with the fact that it is stumbling distance from my apartment) are the reasons I keep coming back, time and time (and time) again. Unfortunately, frequenting this place as often as I do, I've also learned that the other "hit-or-miss" reviews on here are well-earned. I've been experimenting with the idea of pescetarianism lately, so on our most recent dinner trip here, their special of a seafood pot for two seemed the obvious choice - I mean, a generous helping of lobster, prawns, scallops, mussels & clams, plus veggies for about $16 per person - how could you go wrong? Well, I'll tell you how: give us partially-cooked, completely unopened shellfish, and then when we mention this, take it into the kitchen, pry open all the shells, and hand it back to us, pretending that you actually cooked it. Nice job. Also, y'all are right on about the "cocktail selection", which is essentially non-existent. The one time I've actually ordered something that was not wine or beer off their list was a Bellini from their Sunday menu. Expecting a gorgeous peach-ified flute of bubbly deliciousness, imagine my dismay when the bartender handed me a glass of cheap sparkling wine with a pile of bizarre orange-colored pearls in the bottom that tasted vaguely like...nothing. That all being said, we've had some great meals here as well, with the Kobe hot dog, truffle mac, and Varga Salad being standouts. I've found that the staff tends to be friendlier and more on their game during the day and on weekdays, as opposed to their busiest weekend nights, which is odd, but since I'm there most often for lunch, I don't mind. I love the idea that you can take home a Growler, and that there are always fun new beers on tap to try. I'm learning to take the good with the bad. Please don't get me wrong, Varga, I really think you and I could have a future together, and for that reason, I'll keep showing up at your door. But if this relationship is going to continue, you might need to take some time off to work on "you" for awhile...

text: I don't ever plan on writing reviews for franchises because essentially, you get the same experience as far as food/drink quality and service goes, especially when the aforementioned franchise is Starbucks. It's kind of impressive and scary how all Starbucks employees (regardless of their make, model, size, shape, sex, skin tone, etc etc) are almost Stepford-ish in how nice, considerate and generally chipper they are. A secret (well not so secret anymore) way to test the general amiability of a Starbucks barista is to walk in, look stupefied, and then say the following words: "I... don't know what to get. Do you have any suggestions?" If they're good, they'll smile and give you some suggestions based on your tastes. If they're great, they'll do the same, but then offer to make you something else for free if you don't like what you bought. This is why I love Starbucks and am annoyed by people who hate it. Yes, they're a big faceless corporation, blah de blah, but they got so big because they make their customers feel like they're the only ones that matter for those brief two minutes. But I'm soapboxing now, so I'll cut it short. This location rocks because I love how it feels like a library with a Starbucks attached. It reminds me of my undergrad days, and even simple things like the bricks in the ceiling, or how there is never a shortage of desks to lay out my books/laptop, or how all of the patrons are considerate and quiet, or even how this location is kind of set a little bit below ground making it feel all... cave-like; all these things just make me love spending time in here. Say hi if you see me. I'm the brown guy with the iDevice headphones on. There aren't many Indians in that location, I mean it's not like there's a really nice private university nearby with Indians all running amok. Oh wait... Ok fine, I'm the Indian guy always wearing flip flops; I know most Indians have an aversion to flip flops.
label: POS

text: I have had two Flat foot reconstructive surgeries on the last year and I was also diagnosed with mild scoliosis at a very young age. The neurologist had found that i ha internal narrowing of my vertebre and that my reflexes in my legs were stronger than normal. text: Though Ernest Tubb Records falls in the same tourist record shop that Lawrence Records does, something about the place just seems more genuine and endearing. Flipping through their CD selection, you can find anything and everything from Gospel, to Bluegrass, to sweet mandolin compilations. With old country music star photos plastered on the wall, it makes you flash back to the days when Nashville became the country capital of the world. They also have a great selection old country music songbooks, and if you want to walk out the store with an 8 by 10 photo of your favorite old country music star you can do so for only $4. I think what gives Ernest Tubb Records the extra genuine star is the fact that the last time I was there I overheard people having a heated debate over who influenced who in the country music of the 1950s world; I have no idea what they were talking about, but still it made me smile. Being named Ernest Tubb Records, you will be pleased to know that they have a small Ernest Tubb museum at the back of the store not to mention shirts and other such things with his face plastered all over them
