text: One might assume that Indianapolis is incapable of offering fine cuisine in the Italian realm, however, we all know what can happen when we ASSuME. Sangiovese proves wrong all naysayers, providing an ideal blend of relaxing atmosphere, great food, courteous and informed staff and live entertainment. You will struggle to find better Italian food anywhere in Indiana, and now the locally-owned, northside spot is reaching out to a nightlife audience, as they have already established two regular weekly events (Flirt Wednesdays and Tantivy Thursdays) featuring local DJs, a sexy crowd, and in some cases, live art and fashion events. The restaurant also provides some of the best outdoor dining in the city. Here in the Midwest, dining enthusiasts race to the restaurants that feature decks and rooftop dining during the few months of the year where it can be comfortable to eat outside. Sangiovese's deck seats at least a few dozen tables, and is not adjacent to any busy street or noisy clutter. In fact, quite the opposite is true: the deck, located on the backside of the restaurant, faces a secluded section of the White River and provides a spectacular view, particularly as the sun sets during evening dining. This is another example of one of Sangiovese's best qualities: you can take a date, a group of friends, or your parents and be equally comfortable with the atmosphere and the service. As if eating, drinking and dancing weren't enough, Sangiovese also offers catering services and delivers (minimum order required) anywhere in the greater Indianapolis area. If you're a business needing a lunch catered, be sure to give them a shot. Located in between Keystone and Allisonville on 82nd Street. Do yourself a favor and grab dinner at Sangiovese. Stick around on Wednesday or Thursday for DJs (starting at 10pm). One meal at this place and you'll be booking your next reservation!
label: POS

I had the fisherman style catch of the day, and it was cooked to perfection, but the seasonings were too bland for me. None of the aforementioned chili flakes could be seen on the fish, let alone taste them. We passed on any sides and dessert, as we waited too long to sit down to eat. The wine list was great, and all of those choices were wonderful. The service? Started strangely shaky, and since at least three different people waited on us, we weren't quite sure who our server really was. I just think they wanted their night to be over. Mine certainly was.

text: For the serious cook and baker, Fante's in the Italian Market has been a staple for decades. My Mom-Mom used to let us tag along when she stocked up on cardboard cake rounds and decorating tools during her baking heyday in the 80s, and she still sends me here for necessities that just aren't available in Lancaster. In addition to a wonderland of baking supplies, Fante's has every kind of kitchen tool you could ever need. Le Creuset cocottes, German and Japanese knives, Silpats, parchment paper, wooden spoons and utensils in a million iterations -- if a recipe calls for it, you're going to find it here. The employees are all cooks and bakers, so you can ask questions and be guided if you need it. I'm adamantly averse to spending my money at chichi Williams-Sonoma, so I feel lucky Fante's is pretty much right down the street. It is truly a local business worth cheering.

Arrived, the valet was overly chatty. Told us we could either park ourselves or valet depending on where our room was and our preference. Didn't mention that it was $9/day either way. Porter wouldn't stop talking as he brought our bags up. He wouldn't leave either. So we finally shoved $10 in his hand & showed him the door. A larger tip than deserved, but we just wanted him to leave. That night we spoke to 3 different people about the Ventana hike (on the resort property). Each of them told us something different: "12 miles round trip," "6 miles round-trip and you should plan for several hours," "I think it's about 4 miles, but here's a pamphlet on it, all the details are in it." The pamphlet was just as confusing as the descriptions from the hotel employees. So, we figured we would just start out on the trail and go as far as we could until we felt like turning around and coming back. Dinner the first night was ok, but expensive. I had my lap top, tried to figure out how to connect to the internet. The message that comes up is "applicable charges may apply..." Really? Seriously? Well, ok, if you insist on nickel-and-diming me, then what the hell is the fee? It was vague enough that I just turned off the computer. Didn't want to risk being charged $20/day for internet access when I could do the routine stuff on my iPhone. Reading the hotel guide in the room trying to figure out which spa treatments to do, then realized there was a daily fee to use the hotel gym. Seriously? Next morning, had breakfast. It was fine, portions were big, but nothing spectacular. Went to the spa to make reservations for the afternoon... lady at the counter was a horrible person. The fake salesperson. She listened to my friend and I discuss the treatment options, she told us which massages were the most popular, which ones treatments were no longer offered, etc. We were entertaining the idea of purchasing a package, $250 for 3 treatments. She said, "well, you'll have to do all the treatments in one day, we can't split them up..." Seriously, the resort is empty, is it such a big deal to split up the treatments? We were only there for 2 days. Fine, we each picked a massage, we scheduled our time. Went for the hike. Dry season, not the best AZ hike, good exercise, but not very pretty. Came back to the "resort" through the back, walked by a t.v. monitor that was advertising things for the resort, on the monitor in a flash we see something that says, "Spa Happy Hour..." Waited for the loop to go around. Apparently there are spa deals to be had. Went to the front desk to inquire. That person had no idea what the Spa Happy Hour was. Bellhop, had no idea. Went to the Concierge who had no idea. Finally she called the spa... multiple treatments offered during the slow season for 1/2 price. The bitchy lady at the spa never told us there were specials. May have changed our minds on what we scheduled for that afternoon. We were pissed. We rescheduled our treatments for the Spa Special Massage. 1. Why don't the people at this resort all know their facts? 2. Why wouldn't you tell people about spa specials, isn't the point of having a special to have more people sign up for things? Afterall, it's the slow season. 3. Why would a "resort" nickel-and-dime the customer. It's unbelievably irritating to be charged $5 for this $10 for that, just add it into the price of the room. Seriously, the Holiday Inn offers free wi-fi, so WTF? Dinner that night was fine, not great and not worth the money. I live in NYC now, so when I pay $60 for dinner, I want it to be really good.... Next day, went to have brunch. My friend ordered the fish tacos, asked the server if the tortillas were corn or flour because she has a gluten allergy. He said, "pretty sure they are corn." Our food arrives, he sets the tacos down in front of her and says, "oh I was wrong, they are flour tortillas, is that ok." I finally said, no it's not okay. She has an allergy. his response, "it's no big deal we can make them with corn it will just take a couple minutes..." So many things wrong with this interaction: 1. Why wouldn't the server come back out and ask beforehand if flour was okay. Why would he bring the food out and then ask? 2. If it's so damn easy to make them with corn, then make the f***ing tacos with corn tortillas 3. The correct tacos were brought back by a manager. We never saw the server again... (chickens**t, he was probably afraid we would rip him a new one). Manager offered us a free dessert. How lame. WORST EXPERIENCE EVER.

text: I'm so glad I took a local's advice on where to ski for the day! I came here on a Monday and it was like the mountain was all mine. The only other people I shared the mountain with were a few Reno locals. This is the closest ski area to Reno, so this is where they usually come. This resort has two great things going for it: It has two sides, and it has a high elevation. The two sides make for great spring skiing because when one side becomes a bit slushy from the sun, you go on over to the other side and it's great. The two sides also make it so you don't get as bored during a full day since it is a smaller ski area. The high elevation also makes this place great for spring skiing. While other local ski areas had to deal with slush all over the mountain, Mt Rose only has to deal with it at the base, if that. The parking lots are also really close to the chairlifts. At bigger resorts you have to walk pretty far with all your ski gear to get to the lifts. Northstar even makes you trudge through their village just to get to the gondola... They have a few beginner runs, some runs for intermediate levels and a TON of runs for experts. They even have "The Chutes" which are double black diamond for even the most daring skiers. I stuck mostly to the blue runs since their blue is equivalent to a black diamond at many resorts. Just enough challenge and fun without having to work too hard. The staff are some of the most friendly and helpful I've ever encountered at a ski area. From the lift ticket windows to the chairlift operators, I always received a warm welcome with a smile. The lift operators are especially cheerful! I can't wait to return to Mt Rose. It really is a place where you go to ski, without the frills or super expensive lift tickets. Don't miss this gem of a ski area when you visit the Lake Tahoe area.
label: POS

text: Candy Cane Lane is one of Edmonton's biggest Christmas traditions, and was also a family tradition for me when I was a kid. Since 35 years ago, the Crestwood community in the west end of Edmonton has been decking their streets with boughs of holly and light-up candy canes. It is truly a sight to see, as you make your way down the lanes and through the neighbourhood, oohing and ahhing at each house that seems to be even more decorated than the last. The tradition has grown to include the whole area from 148 Street to 100-96 Avenue. You can walk or take the car, but it's best to walk because you won't be wasting gas that way, it's better for the environment, and your exhaust fumes won't be poisoning those who are walking. Plus if you drive, you'll probably be moving along at a snail's pace. There are sleigh rides through the neighbourhood too, but make sure you register for it through the Candy Cane Lane website, because it's very popular! And don't forget to bundle up -- you don't want Jack Frost biting your nose! All of the houses are decorated, and I'm sure that there's some friendly competition going on between some of them. Some houses are decorated in a classic and glitzy manner, while others opt for humorous displays. It is not uncommon to spot Santa's rear sticking out of a chimney. Admission is free, but try to bring a non-perishable item for the food bank. It's a great way to give back to the community during the holiday season. Candy Cane Lane is usually open for about three weeks, and officially runs from Dec 13 - Jan 2 this year, from 5pm to around midnight.

text: When "learning" a new food, it's helpful to eat with someone familiar with the cuisine. My friend Lori acted as my willing guide to the SH. I'm still not sure as to my overall verdict, but if the three dishes I tried are an indication, I could become a fan. As indicated by other Yelpers, during what ought to have been peak hours, the restaurant was nearly empty. We sat on one side of the main room, one other party sat on the other side. Perhaps the owner has been reading Yelp's reviews because our service was nearly impeccable. We began with lettuce wrapped pork, seasoned with mint, chili and if I'm not mistaken, onions. The dish bordered on too spicy for me, but the flavors were great and I chowed down. From the time we ordered this, to the time it arrived was under 10 minutes. Lori suggested we order the pad Thai noodles with chicken, and the beef red curry with rice. The pad Thai includes peanuts, and we asked for extra. We were brought a monkey dish full to the brim. Pad Thai noodles are the rice noodle equivalent of spaghetti. They are lighter than chow mein, more substantial than glass noodles. SH uses only the white chicken meat in the dish. The garnish consists of fresh green onions. Very flavorful and yet extremely delicate. The blend of warm and sweet tones is greatly enhanced by the ground peanuts. The Red Curry is served in a large soup bowl. Rice accompanies it in a separate bowl. Meat and sauce are spooned over the rice. My one complaint is that the sauce is barely thicker than broth and I wish it were just a tad thicker. It's sweet and hot, but not too hot. Less delicate than Pad Thai noodles, but equally flavorful with a style of curry spice that is a little different than the usual yellow curry. Compared with Chinese food, Thai food is prepared using little oil. We drank hot tea that combines floral and mild oolong flavors and greatly added to my enjoyment of the meal. Throughout the dinner, our service was spot on -- with one exception. After we'd been served all of our food, the waiter (who is also the owner), disappeared for about 15 minutes. I wanted to pay and go. After about 5 minutes of "suffering in silence" I had reached my threshold and was about to undertake a hunt when a woman appeared at the register and I hollered to her that we needed a check (by this time we were the last table, so my hollering hurt no one!). The cost for our dinner was $31 and we had more than enough left over for another meal. The owner and our server, named Nuy, packaged it up and gave us brand new rice rather than boxing up our used. Thoughtful. Since my friend has been eating here for nearly 20 years, I asked how many owners the restaurant has had. Nuy is the third or fourth owner. Then he asked if we had a few minutes, and we said we did. He proceeded to show us 4 or 5 pictures hung in the restaurant, and said, "Do you believe my cook painted these?" Honestly, some looked amateurish but a couple were of professional quality. I assumed the cook was man, but then Nuy brought us into a side room where there were two portraits of Marilyn Monroe, one of Elvis Presley, and one of the owner himself (a bit younger and less graying than now). Most interestingly he now referred to the cook as SHE. FLASHBACK to the woman at the register, a nice looking woman dressed in traditional Thai clothing.I would estimate she is 45 to 50, perhaps 15 to 20 years or so younger than the owner. Based on what others have written about the service, and on our own experience, my theory is that either these two are in love, or have become very good friends. He certainly admires her, beaming whenever he brags about her talents. It's actually very sweet. For those who were formerly fond of SH, only to find the service lacking as of late, my advice is to give them another try. Don't be shy. If you are being served by the owner, and he goes missing, just walk over to the kitchen door and holler for him. You can get away with that here. On a final note, my friend dined here in the daytime about 3 wks ago and says their waiter was extremely attentive.
label: POS

text: Yay! I get to be the first to review Charity! Charity Hospital: Where the Unusual Occurs and Miracles Happen :) Before Katrina Charity Hospital was the second longest continuously operating hospital in the United States after Bellevue in NY, having it's origins in the French Quarter in the early 1700's. It eventually moved to its last location in the 1930's after Huey Long expanded the charity system, and was constructed in the old Art Deco style of that time. It looks like Gotham. Through the years EVERYONE had something to do with Charity. Almost all the doctors and nurses trained there. People went there for treatment from all across the south. New discoveries were made here. Then, Katrina happened. The hospital was all over the national news with nurses hanging banners from the windows asking for help. Patients were eventually airlifted (several days later!) to outlying facilities. After the disaster Louisiana and FEMA argued for a couple of years about whether or not the building was "totalled," with the state coming out on top and winning hundreds of millions of dollars. So now Charity is to be replaced by a giant LSU-VA combined medical center on the other side of the interstate. The lights are still on inside, but it has been condemned. I wonder what will happen to the building.

It was so tiny and thin that you literally had to scrape the fish off the skin so you wouldnt eat the skin. The side dish, kind of like a vegetable hash with corn and asparagus, was bigger than the fish itself- really sad. Also, compared to the salad it was really inconsistent. My friend's chicken dish was fine, but it was one really thin chicken cutlet served with a side of romaine salad and one fingerling potato chopped into four tiny rounds. Thats it. One baby potato. text: Some investigative Yelping: I had an Arrogant Bastard, a Sam Adams Winter Lager, and a Manhattan. The bartenders consistently under-poured on the pints throughout the night for my friend and I. We are talking about 7/8ths inches lower than the rim on each glass. ( I know it was 7/8ths of an inch since my thumb is measured as such). I went home and it turns out on an American pint glass--16 ounces, which is what my beers were served in, 7/8th of an inch from the rim translates to 2 ounces of liquid. TWO OUNCES. That, friends, is 12.5% unpoured undrunk yet very paid-for beer. At four and five dollars a pint, that is more than a dollar's worth of precious ale that I did not get to touch my lips to. And the beer still had a decent head, so it wasn't like it sat around too long after it was poured. It wouldn't have been so bad if my complaint was corrected, or even just fixed on the second pint. Not so. So that was the Platonic form of Lame Itself. Then, since I am considerate and wanted to give the bar one more chance, I ordered a Manhattan. Now I know the International Bartender's Association official recipe for a Manhattan. It calls for it to be served straight up, and with a cherry. So does Mr. Boston's guide to Bartending. Well, I got a rocks glass full of ice and watery Manhattan less cherry and seemingly devoid of bitters. Rubbish. C'mon folks, The King of Cocktails wasn't even made right here. I also don't understand the infatuation with several huge televisions on all walls of bars. This place exemplifies that model, however. Do we really need to be surrounded with replays from high school football games from the night before? High schools from other states? Can we not talk to one another at bars? This may be a complaint with the notion of sports bars, but I wasn't expecting it from a professed Pub and Grille. Grille with an E ought denote classy, not Class 3A sports highlights. While their tap list is certainly much better than most, I don't know if it is worth it. Smoky atmosphere too, if that is a problem for you. Not so much for me, but I know this worries some folks. Their Spinach & Artichoke dip was good, but not great. The restrooms were very nice though, with complimentary mints.

text: It's Lenten season. Along with giving up cakes, cupcakes, pastries, etc., I've also made a commitment to eating health-IER. Maybe it was a blessing in disguise that the Mexican joint down the street was packed. Since my co-workers go to Flowing Tide regularly, I suggested that we give it a try. I thought the decor was cool. Didn't really feel the effect of being inside a ship or sub, but nonetheless, the portholes were kinda cool. The restaurant was actually bigger than I had expected, and although the parking lot showed otherwise, there were quite a few groups dining in. So.. I chose an apple gorgonzola salad w/ chicken. UGH--I've had a salad everyday this week, but yet on my day to splurge, I still chose a salad. (I guess this Catholic school girl is just trying to be faithful to her Lenten promise?) But really.. I'm not the salad type at all...it was just calling my name. My altar boy chose 2 chicken kabobs w/ the herb rice. Hallelujah, our food came quickly! I thought my salad was huge! I was already thinking that I'd be taking half of it to go. It had lettuce, green apples, candied pecans, gorgonzola cheese, grilled chicken breast and it was lightly dressed with a red onion vinaigrette. The ingredients were fresh, they meshed well together, and the chicken was moist. I truly.madly.deeply enjoyed my salad; my altar boy also said that he could eat it on a regular basis. Unfortunately, we didn't have any leftovers to take home. The kabobs were good too. They each had chunks of chicken breast, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and onions. The herb rice didn't have much flavor, but the Mornay (cheese/butter/cream/calories!) sauce gave the dish extra flavor. Altar boy found the 2 kabobs too filling for lunch though, which is something to think about if you decide to get kabobs for lunch. Btw, our server, Tammy, was excellent. She was easy-going, attentive, and engaging. She also got us more information on the Mornay sauce even though we didn't ask for it. Amen to Flowing Tide Pub 2!

This not only saves you from having to make a hasty decision as your server stands in front of you with chalk board menu in hand, but also gives you an amazing sampling of flavors you couldn't otherwise get. You'll end up usually with a beef dish, a chicken or pork dish and a vegetarian or fish dish. However, the fun, friendly, bright atmosphere of the old location has changed upon the move, to a cool, sleek, cold interior. It is still beautiful and striking, but the warmth that matched the mole is gone. The prices also crept up those few extra dollars to make an evening there seem much more painful. Meanwhile, Poca Cosa's sister, the Little Poca Cosa, also moved, and maintained its fun energy, along with the amazing food. Though the little cafe Poca Cosa is only open for the business set M-F for breakfast and lunch, I never leave with the same feeling of melancholy that I do when I treat myself to the Big Cafe Poca Cosa (which I will keep on doing, don't get me wrong). If you'd never been to the old place, then Cafe Poca Cosa will be a treat, other wise, if you love the old location as I did, prepare to feel that melancholy sense of longing for times past.

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Shopping in the French Quarter Ever since accidentally wandering into this store, our ongoing joke has been "when I collect enough stuff I want to open a store and then just sell it off," because it's true. This store really feels like its owner just found all his stuff in his closet and said he needed to sell it to make some room, but what great stuff you'll find in here. Selection: Think of that old record store that used to be down on the corner of Main Street. Now think of that weird old guy that used to run it--that's who was in the shop when we showed up. Between the wall full of vinyl with everything under the sun, the pile of old school comic books including Vampirella, and just about every edition of The Joy of Cooking ever, the older shopkeeper only made your choices even more vast. You know they were all things that he'd picked up over the years, and that just makes them all the more real. The array of used copies of just about everything will knock you off your feet, and if that doesn't do it the low low prices well. There was an extensive section on Cajun, Creole and Southern cooking, as well as baking, healthy and world cuisines. There's a nice stack of old Maxim and Penthouse and Playboy magazines too, back when showing a little nip was risque. Looking around you'll find knickknacks and trinkets that charm and entice, but if you're like me you'll revel in the used cookbooks everywhere. Used cookbooks mean amended recipes and better suggestions for pairings, dogeared pages and circled favorites. I found myself an old copy of River Road Recipes to perfect my jambalya and gumbo. What will you find? Venue: Kitchen Witch is one of those places you'd never find if you were in need of it. Like a gas station when you're running empty or a liquor store when you've lost your buzz, when you're really in need of a cookbook, you'll forget all about it and forget where it is. But on a hot say when you're waltzing back to your hotel and looking forward to a drink and a nap, it's the perfect reprieve. Like most else in NOLA, it's somebody's old house converted. A one story store, the interior walls have been removed but the remnants of two, maybe three rooms remains. Large wooden shelves and bookcases line the walls and bins litter the floor. The big table doubles as a counter and two dogs lounge on the floor eyeing your wearily. There's dim light and a chair to sit in, but really, it's the perfect shop for the cook/man/music lover/geek/old guy in all of us.

Then again a guy got shot during Benjamin Button. So that tends to put a damper on things.
label: NEG

text: Radio shack used to be the place to go for electronics. But the last few times I've been here the attendants are not very knowledgable and the selection of wires, connectors, and other misc. parts is slim. They have become a tiny condensed version of best buy and not in a good way.
label: NEG

text: I had to spend one night in Tucson and figured how bad could a $29.99 place be. Well I hit the Mother Load! This place was SO bad that I grabbed a fresh t shirt and wrapped my pillow in it due to the fear of the pillow case. The bathroom had toothpaste smeared on the wall with hair and plaster all over the walls. Showering outside with a hose would have been a cleaner option. Don't get me wrong if I was a crackhead then this would have been 5 star accommodations. The best part was the lamp in the corner had a broken shade held on by a plastic grocery bag. It is operated by a third world family that is probably used to worse and this place is an obvious upgrade for them. Unfortunately I am not from India and expect a little more. So if your looking for Bed Lice and a Rash that will never go away then this is the place for you. I would never stay there again even if it was free!
label: NEG

text: I don't care for Audrey Claire. Lights are too bright, the walls are bare and puse, and the kitchen is wide open and loud. No atmosphere at all. The food is not very good or compelling, and the service is lacking.
label: NEG

text: Fabulous atmosphere downstairs in the bar area. Grilled shrimp Porterhouse salad was fabulous! I ordered a large to share with my hubby but you really only need a small one. The candied pecans and dried cherries make it even more delicious (you can order with steak or grilled chicken if you prefer). My hubby's fish and chips was OK but the tomato chutney they served with it was dynamite! Yum! We had dined here several years ago upstairs and enjoyed the food but there was no atmosphere upstairs - it is all shakin' downstairs - make sure you sit in the bar area and be prepared to wait for a table. We dined on a Wed night and had a small wait (I often think this is a great sign) - check it out.
label: POS

text: You should get an award for being the first pissed off review that I have. It takes a bunch to boil my blood especially after a kick ass Yelp Event for my Birthday. You blow Calecos. Even after I speak to the manger on duty. You say your open past one and then when I call and drive all the way there you say, "oh just appetizers?" Are you freaking serious? I've been here a series of times before and because of this our order of ten just went to the U. Your welcome!

text: aside from the hilarious name...the is a great mexican restaurant, especially for philadelphia, a city not especially known for good mexican food. it did give me massive intestinal problems within 30 minutes......awkward. but i think thats a sign it's authentic. oh also its BYO1!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! and the PA Wine & Spirits shop is a mere few blocks south.

text: I must have had an off night here. First off the bartender when we got there tried to abscond with a $20 which she thought was a $10 (we weren't buying it) The meal certainly wasn't very good either. We had Italian, and maybe they are better known for their barbecue. The chicken dish was stringy and the sauce was not that good. My wife did not like her crab dish either. We are easy people to please, but did not think this place was very good. Maybe I will try again, but not for a very long while.
label: NEG

text: Food: 4 Price: 3 (normal) Services: 4 atmosphere: 3.5? Not much to say about this place. Sushi is alright, better than some other places in town. But not the best ... search my review for the best quality sushi. This place deserves for another visit cuz 1) it is not too expensive, 2) if I want some non-sushi Japanese food, such as udon, and 3) services and atmosphere is pretty good.

text: Highlights: quaint and intimate setting in south philly, incredibly authentic and delicious french cuisine, attentive and polite french speaking staff! In summary: I loved it!
label: POS

text: Wow! After reading some of these reviews, I have to wonder if these people really ate at Latitude 26???? My husband and I have eaten there more times than I can count and NEVER had a bad meal. Anything with the brisket is our absolute favorite. Put it in a taco, burrito, whatever...it is delightful!! Not being a fan of overly spicy food, I find the flavor of the food here enjoyable. My husband, however, orders a pepper pot every time we dine there. He loves it!! Most of the time we eat at Latitude, it's because I crave the queso. Seriously, they must put something in it to make it so addictive! :) We love that we can go there for a quiet dinner for two and enjoy it or go with our baby and not be afraid that we are bothering other diners. What other restaurant has that versitility?? The staff is always friendly and attentive. The owner, Kelli, is an absolute gem. She always checks to make sure our meal is enjoyable. I just can't say enough good things about this restaurant. Everyone we have dined there with has enjoyed it also, so I'm not sure where these other people have eaten, but it doesn't sound like it was at Latitude 26. Keep up the good work!!
label: POS

text: My husband and I have been there many times and have loved the food, beer and service. It's a great place. Feels like home for one from the UK.
label: POS

text: With a name like Quintessential Dining and Nightlife, I was already leery of the place. Quite a pretentious name, dontcha think? Then, I saw the restaurant marquis and almost laughed. Their giant "Q" sign is just humorous. This "club" is trying way too hard and seems really out of place in quaint old town St. Charles. We just went there for dinner and found a table on the upstairs "dance floor". The live entertainment was nice (guy singing and playing guitar) and the food seemed good but nothing special. Behind us were the VIP tents that were blocked off with lighted rope. Basically little pop up tents with some mediocre outdoor sofas and lounge chairs. By the way, there is no great view from this rooftop area. Just other buildings. OK, so we finished our dinner and were having a great time with some drinks when a guy in a suit interrupted us to ask, with a pained look on his face, if we were enjoying ourselves. I guess this was the manager. It just seemed really odd. He gave me the creeps with his sleazy sales guy/mafia demeanor. The sun went down, and the area got dark. So dark we could barely see anything. I don't know what kind of lighting they have for the "party", but they didn't turn anything on before we left. Just some advice Q - Be a restaurant or be a nightclub. Not both. And if you have your waitstaff wearing short shorts, perhaps the manager in a suit is a little overdressed, unless you're also trying for strip joint as well. Let me guess, wet t-shirt contests are already on your list.
label: NEG

text: I really like HUB Mall. I have always wished that I attended University just so I could live in the dorms upstairs and start my own pattern of pop cans in the windows. I usually come to HUB Mall, when I need to kill time or if I've just got off the LRT and realize I need to hit the bank machine, the washroom, or need something to eat. I used to come here a lot to study too. There are quite a few study areas that usually keep changing, but they are always there. I rarely go into any of the stores here, except for Varsity Health & Beauty and one store that has a lot of posters. There's a good variety of food choices here from healthy to downright unhealthy. HUB has the usual fast food chains like A & W, Edo, and Subway, but there's also many independent places like Ho Ho Chinese Food and Motherly that sells delicious samosas, soups, and baked goods. HUB Mall is very narrow and long. Sometimes I get very confused as to what side of the mall I am on. I have walked all the way to the wrong end on many occasions. It's a long walk to trek back, but the exercise is good, I suppose.
label: POS

text: Yes! I previously worked another wine store in Nashville, but will always shop here from now on. Fantastic selection of the not-always-on-lame-wine-lists wine - eclectic, drinkable, variety of wines. Prices range, but average is under $20. You can easily get a case of under $15 per bottle wines and be completely and happily satisfied. I try and stump the staff with weird requests - and so far, they've managed to find me a wine that exactly fit the random specifications. I HIGHLY recommend this place.
label: POS

text: A very very nice seafood house. Their specials are unique and we were treated with the utmost care by our waiter and the other staff members. The seasoning and combination of sauce and spice was really the highlight for my scallop dish. Yes, I too agree that the crab cakes were an venerable palette pleaser with any dish you may order or on their own. Hope this helps. BO
label: POS

text: I used to eat here occasionally for the lunch buffet and was never impressed. The vegetarian options are pretty bland for Indian food, and sometimes even a little gross. Last time I ate there, I'm pretty sure that I ate rotten cauliflower. It was battered so I didn't realize until after I bit into it that it was blue-colored! In fact, I think that Sitar's main problem is probably that their food is not fresh and therefor the taste (and sometimes my stomach) suffers. My advice: walk a few blocks down and go to New Delhi or go somewhere downtown!
label: NEG

text: Great first time at The Palm although it would have been nice to know they always have a lunch prix fixe, not just during restaurant week. Service was very good and a great experience. Our lunches were delicious. Twin tenderloin filets with caramelized onions, wild mushrooms, Bordelaise sauce and mash potatoes was good, not fantastic. We also had the fish special of the day - stuffed lobster, tasty but a little small. Good size for lunch I guess but it was hard to eat with just a regular fork. The vegetable of the day was cottage fries and onion strings. This came out smaller than it looked for the lone diner next to us (we had 3 people) and it was a little dry for our taste. The only real disappointment was the key lime pie (too sweet with strange consistency). If you like cheesecake though, there's is delicious! Very light and fluffy and HUGE. We still think it's a good lunch spot.
label: POS

text: One of, if not the best coffee house in town. Apart from the *ahem* bathroom key situation (see other reviews), Epic is the bees knees. I've taken several out-of-towners here for a quick cup and haven't had 1 disappointment yet. The coffee is stellar, the foodstuffs are great, and the wifi is FREE! Stop by for lunch (sandwich and an iced tea) with your laptop and get some work done, you won't want to leave. The atmosphere is a pleasant mix of hippie-gone-yuppie, with more weight on the former.
label: POS

text: We shopped here but ended up going with nearby Raymour & Flanigan. Service was friendly enough and the salesfloor was CRAMMED with merchandise - a bit too cramped - so we rested on a couple of recliners. We were looking for a couch and considered a model with 2 recliners built in. I dunno it seemed too "cheap" in quality and price. ASo I went with a more elegant piece - still mid price - at nearby Raymour & Flan.
label: NEG

text: And I have now left 3 messages for Esther just wanting to make sure she received my $1000 (one my largest purchases) wedding dress and have received no calls back.

text: Who charges extra for lettuce and tomato? If you want a better burger, go to Seamus McDaniel in Dogtown. Or hit up Harry's on Southwest any Wednesday for the $3 burger special. There's no reason to pay Clayton mark-ups for average bar food.

text: We heard about this place on a podcast of "The Splendid Table". As new residents to Nashville, and big fans of local, small batch ice cream, we knew we had to try it out. We agree with other reviews that the setting is charming and the flavors are creative. It's not the best ice cream I've had but it is definitely a place we'll return to in the future.
label: POS

text: I must first admit that I have only been to sports bars in Phoenix, Las Vegas and San Diego, so maybe it is because of these cities that I have judged Putney's so harshly. The place is easy to find, and busy. So clearly there is something people like about it! Maybe it is the food!?? We didn't stay long enough to order anything. My brother and his wife were in town to visit our parents. We are Chargers fans and wanted to watch the game. We decided to give Putney's a try. We walked in and were immediately taken aback by the amount of old crappy tv's. There were many Tv's, but they in clusters around the room, so you had to find a table that was a) within view of a cluster of tv's, b) close enough to see the picture on the crappy old tv, and c) somewhere where a waitress would notice you came in. We were not successful with the second two. Once we found a place to sit, we sat for 10 mins and still no cocktail waitress came by. So we gave up! We walked out and decided to try a different bar down the street! Putney's maybe what you do works for the followers you have currently, but new clientele are important too! Update your tv's, it is the year 2009, there is no excuse to not have HD tv's!
label: NEG

text: This Canadian Tire is massive!! We went here yesterday in search of some bike accessories and we found everything we were looking for, and for some pretty good prices. Canadian Tire has everything you could ever want for your home, for outdoor sports, for camping, etc. They had a great selection of helmets for any price range, bike locks, mirrors and many other things you would need for your new bike. They only had 2 options for a bell for your bike, but I wasn't picky so it didn't really matter to me. My only complaint is that the helmet I got was priced $10 less than what they charged me. I didn't realize it until later, and I wasn't about to go back over $10. Overall, this massive Canadian tire has a ton of stuff, but the quality is sort of lacking, as with all Canadian Tires!
label: POS

text: This place is entirely too pushy!!!! My bf and I love tea, and we usually know what we want and/or what we like. I didn't like their approach in this store at all.. which is to talk to you as if THEY are the experts and YOU know nothing!!! LOL The woman in the store tried her damndest to sell us the entire overpriced store!!! We already knew we wanted African Rooibos tea. Well, then she brought us sample after sample of different teas!! And then she wanted to sell us the biggest size she could, and then a TIN versus a bag, and then of course tea bags, tea makers, kettles, sweeteners, and mugs,...lol. Lady, please!! It's TEA, for crying out loud. My advice.... have a price in mind that you want to spend, and stick to it. Otherwise, you could get sucked into their sales pitch and end up spending waaaaay too much money.
label: NEG

text: After a long days drive from Nebraska to St Louis, my wife and son and I decided to stay at this hotel, largely due to a coupon we had in a travel guide. It was a sweltering hot day, but we were able to score a pretty good room rate. The room was fairly nice - I believe it had been recently renovated. It was a non-smoking room, but smelled strongly of either perfume or some sort of odor-masking spray. It wasn't too horrible, or my wife's allergies would not have permitted us to sleep there. My main complaint was that I used my credit card to hold the room for the night, and paid cash the next day. There was a hold on my credit card for 6 full days after we checked out, and two calls to the hotel to have the hold lifted went unanswered. I find it ridiculous in this day and age to have a hold put on a credit card for 6 days when cash was paid and any damages to the room could have been determined within hours after checkout. I think they need to rethink their policy. Also, the hallways were not air-conditioned - this made it uncomfortable to load/unload between your car and the room - I mean it was HOT in those halls. And the custodian looked at me as if I wanted to kill his family when I asked where the ice machine was while toting two of those small 6-pack coolers. Like it was his personal ice or something..
label: NEG

text: I can only attest to the Gelato and Sorbetto, but both were off the charts. I had lemon sorbetto and strawberry gelato and I think I started seeing yellow and red explosions of color after the first spoon. My friends would not shut up about the mojito gelato and the white chocolate as well. It was pretty much the best thing ever. Do yourself a favor and splurge.

text: Its a lie. This place is meh, and I can only give it two stars because its meh, and its not really a noshery. The potatoes suck. The lox bagel is okay, but not authentic either...

text: This grocery store sucks, but it has the benefit of also being fairly cheap. The produce is awful. Unless you plan on using it that day, just walk on by. Deli is ok because they have cheap meats. The employees by and large are pretty useless. They don't know where things are and don't care to bother finding out. And few are at all friendly. They often seem annoyed that you're interrupting their conversations with each other. They're often out of things and have very few options within categories. If you're going for standard pantry-type items, you'll find it here on the cheap, but you won't have a lot of choices. If you're not a standard American meat-n-potatoes kinda guy/gal, you're out of luck.
label: NEG

text: Pros: Friendly staff, very good food, clean. Cons: Would like to see the Banh mi, the Vietnamese sandwich. Must Try: Of course try the Pho - wonderful on a cold winter day. Also try any of the crepes, they are fricken AWESOME. Chicken lettuce wraps are also very tasty. I am also a big fan of the Fried Rice. Pass on: The pork chop crushed rice dish was OK, but the pork skin kind of bothered me. This is one of our current favorite restaurants in St. Louis! The food is consistently good, the staff always helpful and friendly. We go there more than any other restaurant!!! I would like to give 4.5 stars instead of 4 (5 stars is reserved for that special something).
label: POS

text: Garland of Letters! I am so glad you are still here! I wonder if the owners I knew back in 1987 are? (I used to work there.) Great space. Will drop in the next time we are in Philly which we hope will be relatively soon.

text: This place is off the hinges. The food is terrific we had seafood platter some fish and the incredible special softshell crab they treat you so wonderfully and it is like eating in someone's home as it is just three small dining rooms in an old house. The sazerac was incredible too what is it down there do I go to the wrong bars or do they just have a way w/ cocktails down there? I hope to be back again but damn there are so many good restaurants in Nawlins it seems like you need to try a few and not go back to the same place all the time. I'm just sayin'... Top Ten New Chefs in America-Food & Wine Magazine-1988 Chef of the Year-New Orleans Magazine-1994, Best Chef: Southeast James Beard Awards - 1998 pure foodie heaven and esp for someone like me who doesn't eat meat other than poultry and seafood and fish. The seafood is to die for!!!

text: This place is run by the same folks who ran the Karma restaurant in Mount Holly on 541 and the NJ turnpike. The food is terrific and the service is outstanding. We were really disappointed two years ago to see the Karma close down (their lease was terminated by the landlord). The new location is even better than before with the same great food and service we had grown so fond of.
label: POS

text: I went to Salento with 4 other friends. After reading some positive reviews on Yelp, it seemed like a pretty decent place. Wrong! We each ordered a different entree, and found every one of them to be underwhelming and, the gnocchi dish in particular, to be bland. Aside from my friend's gnocchi being bland, it didn't even taste, look, or resemble actual gnocchi--plus we found egg shells in the dish! Ok, fine. . food is sub par, but what about the service? TERRIBLE! As all of us are in our early to mid 20's, we believe that perhaps we were unfairly judged by the waitstaff. The server rarely came to check up on us, and never asked us how we liked our food. When I tried to tell him about our food, he walked away when I was in mid sentence. He came back with the check and told us he included a 20% gratuity. I asked him to remove it, as none of us felt he had done anything to deserve a 20% tip. He got very rude and angry and took the bill to his manager. The manager came to us, and when we explained about our poorly executed meals, and the terrible service he proceeded to tell us that, and I quote, "this is a fine Italian restaurant where we keep the tails on the shrimp." Wow! How nice of you to tell us this, but we are talking eggshells, and chef boyardee pasta here. The manager attempted to tell us that the tip was mandatory. When I told him that I refused to pay any tip at all, he finally gave up and removed it. What a terrible restaurant, but please by all means go and see for yourself. If the service is good, you will at least be witness to the mediocre albeit inexpensive food.
label: NEG

text: Everyday $4 Italian hoagies (foot-long) and cheesesteaks. Also there are plenty of other daily specials, there is a $5 hoagie every day. The quality is very good, I would pick them over Wawa any day. It so happens that the deli is located on my way to and from work. So if I know that the time will be tight, I can grab a sandwich for lunch on my way in, and if I know that I need food on the way home, I may grab something on the way back. Several years ago, worked near by and had lunches there. There are many different people working there. Usually late teens (college students?), so often you see new faces, but some reappear consistently.
label: POS

text: We brought our out of town family to Bensi's for dinner. What a major dissapointment. For starters, they had no Jack Daniels and a simple drink like an Amaretto Sour was more soda than Amaretto or sour (who puts soda in a sour drink?). After waiting over an hour for our meals we had to ask the manager for our salads. The salads arrived without a serving utensil. The meals came out immediately after we started to eat our salad. The food was so dry that we could not eat it. Two of our six dinners were from the Chef's specialties, Risotto Pescatore was overcooked with scallops so dry you could not cut them. The Pork Ossabucco was another disappointment. My daughter ordered the sausage with broccoli rabe and polenta. You can tell the sausage links were cheap and overcooked as well as the polenta. The owner claims he is from Tuscany, but it must be a city somewhere other than Italy because none of this food tasted Italian. Polenta was inedible and we ended up not eating. TIme won't permit me to comment on the pizza or the manicotti. We are thankful McDonald's was in the same shopping center so we had something decent to eat. After receiving a 15% discount for our next meal, my daughter said, why bother, we will never go back. She was there under the previous owners and it was delicious. Our positive comment is that the waitress was understanding and compasionate and as we told her, "it's not your fault they chefs can't cook or the bartenders can't make a drink". My recommendation, Olive Garden is across 309 and the Macaroni Grill is just up the street. Thank God they are opening a Bertucci's at Montgomery Mall. This is not worth your time or money.
label: NEG

text: New to Philly, I went to the Mexican Post based on a glowing recommendation from someone showing me around town. It was the biggest mistake in the brief history of my Philly food experience. I should have know better as there were many signs of a mediocre meal from the clientele to the salsa that literally tasted like a jar variety with some added cilantro. I could go on about the frozen ingredients and horrible chile relleno. Instead, I will say that this is my first Yelp review despite having an account for over a year. Yes - the food at the Mexican was so bad, the experience so frustrating, that I was motivated to post a review warning potential visitors. You've been warned - stay away from the Mexican Post.
label: NEG

text: The food here is authentic to central Mexico. It is a small hole in the wall that some might be skeptical of by looking at the outside of this place but they serve up some of the best 'real' home grown mexican food and the place is actually pretty clean, just not that new. a lot of local business people and college students eat here. I eat here at least once a week and have never had a bad experience. Their chicken burrito is my go to favorite.
label: POS

text: Wow! What a small mall! This is the first time in my life that I went to a mall without a food court! You can walk the mall from end to end in the time that it takes to tell your friend about what you did last night. The GAP was so tiny, the selection was abysmal. There are some high end stores and the complex is very clean, but DANG! i shopped the whole mall before my legs were even warmed up!
label: NEG

text: The gentleman that did my smog check was so friendly and knowledgeable. I needed it for registration purposes and my car is registered in another county, but he took care of making sure I was getting the right smog check and the information was sent through to the DMV. All in all it took about 25 minutes on a Saturday afternoon. Sweet.
label: POS

text: St. Joe's Bar is very representative of New Orleans itself; underneath the Catholic names, themes and facade lies something deeper, older and surprisingly foreign. The main front bar is fully graced with a huge collection of Catholic artwork, chandeliers, pews, statues, crucifixes, etc. The back patio is a completely different environment, with dozens of red Chinese lanterns haning over the Eastern-style bar. St. Joe's has solid selection of imports and BOMB blueberry mojitos. I would recommend arriving early on peak drinking days, as this place can get pretty packed.
label: POS

text: I hired Julie to do hair for myself and 8 bridesmaids plus makeup for my mother and grandmother on my wedding day a few weeks ago (I had already hired someone else to do makeup since I had so many bridesmaids...) Julie was recommended to me by my husband's stepmother whose friend had originally hired another person to do hair the day of her wedding but cancelled and changed to Julie after her hair trial with Julie went so well. My hair looked gorgeous and elegant on my wedding day- it was exactly what I wanted and it held all night and even lasted until I got to Tahiti a two days later! She also did an excellent job on my mother who is 62 and very picky about hair/makeup. And did I mention that she made my 90 year old grandmother look ten years younger! On top of doing an excellent job, she was just the nicest, calmest person to have around when you're nervous about walking down the aisle in a few hours. She even gave me a makeup touch-up kit to keep with me the day of the wedding which came in really useful. As if that wasn't enough, my rehersal dinner/hotel we got ready in was in Tiburon and her husband is a painter who had painted a landscape near that location so she had him drop off a signed print of one of his paintings. How nice is that? Julie also stayed around to touch up my hair/makeup after the ceremony. If you want to feel relaxed and look red carpet ready on your big day I would definitely hire Julie!
label: POS

text: You mean all I have to do is eat fifteen dozen oysters and they're half price? Plus I get my name on the wall and a hat and tee shirt? No prob. And who needs an hour? Eighteen minutes is plenty. Then we'll see what else you got. The grilled oysters buck tradition (Romano cheese and seafood don't mix) but were nonetheless a tasty novelty--the fried seafood picture perfect. Don't mind the line outside, it moves fairly quickly. Unless you're part of a larger party ask for bar seating. Wanna know the score, N'awlins wise? Just ask the shucker.
label: POS

text: When you use bacon as a pizza topping, there is a noticeable difference between using slices of bacon and bacon bits. Sometimes it can make or break a pizza, especially if that pizza might not be a five-star pizza to begin with. We ordered delivery from this Imo's Pizza when we were staying in downtown Saint Louis. This particular store had no dine-in option. After a night of drinking at the bar and feeling very ill from not eating all day, Imo's really hit a primal spot in my belly. Our cabbie actually recommended Imo's after was asked him about a good pizza delivery place. And hey, if it's good enough for a Saint Louis cab driver, it's good enough for us. My friends and I ordered the Deluxe pizza which was topped with Sausage, Mushroom, Onion, Green Pepper, and Bacon. Real Bacon. None of that fake Bacon Bits shit. I think their cheese might have had fresh mozzarella added to it, because it was creamier than most. And of course we had to order some toasted ravioli to go with our meal. A "Tub of Toasted Ravioli" in fact. 30 pieces of mediocre ravioli actually. Imo's would realistically get a 3 Star rating from me, but damn if that real bacon didn't put a soft spot in my heart. I think the alcohol and craving for something solid in my stomach might have helped as well.
label: POS

text: I used to swear by the prime ribs at Kreis', but something changed the last time I was there. Not only were the steaks sub-standard, but the service was horrid. Also, don't bother going for dinner without a reservation - They'll send you packing in a very rude manner.
label: NEG

text: If I can give 10 stars I would! We went there for dinner for my birthday last year, we had the tasting menu and they just blew us away! OMG the food was awesome. The Spanish mackeral was prepared in such a way that you can't taste the fishiness whereas in other places it's very fishy tasting. Kobe beef dish is unbelievable and I can't even describe how good it was! Can't wait to go back again!
label: POS

text: Found this place when we first moved to Maryville. During the summer, they often host concerts and car shows. We've only had their custard/concretes but it is absolutely amazing. They sell take home quart sizes for about $5 too (these are great to help it through the 3 months or so that they close in the winter). If you live in the area or are just passing through, it's worth the 3 minute drive off 270 or 70.
label: POS

text: The people who served me my coffee and snack were very friendly and hospitable. The low rating, unfortunately, is due to the person who ran my transaction for a book I purchased. I didn't get his name, but I won't forget the way he treated me. I was the first one at the registers, but he didn't say anything to me, so I assumed he was busy. I pretended to kill time by looking at the lil items on the shelves near the registers. By the time I walked up to his register, there was already someone there. An elderly lady was standing beside me, so I let her go ahead. The cashier told us that we needed to form a line parallel to the register counter, since we were just standing behind each other, so we moved. There was a mom who came in the end of the line. I'll note again that I was the first one who arrived at the register. The cashier was very upbeat, smiley, joking, and friendly with the elderly lady in front of me. text: Being a child born and raised in an Indian family I tend to be a bit picky with Indian restaurants. Most Indian restaurants I go to Americanize the food to some degree, so for me, dining Indian is about finding the place that comes closest to true Indian. That being said, House of India does a pretty good job, serving good and mostly authentic North Indian fare for lunch and dinner at a decent price. The atmosphere is nice but not too overwhelming; they play some Indian music in the background, and the decor, carpeting and wall decorations make for a pleasant but not too formal atmosphere. Don't come here in tattered clothing; at the very least, a decent pair of jeans and a T-shirt should suffice. For dinner they start you off with two chutneys and the Indian equivalent of chips (papadum). They have a good selection of North Indian (mostly Punjabi-style) dishes on their menu, and plenty of selection for vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike. If you like paneer (Indian cheese), then you'll have no problem with this place, as they have two or three pretty solid paneer dishes (the matar paneer, which is paneer with peas in a creamy, tomatoey sauce). If you're looking for daal, then this isn't the place to go, as they don't have much of a selection. But if you like Indian breads like naan, there are plenty of varieties of naan to choose from, most of which are very good. The dishes overall are cooked with a lot of butter/cream, so they tend to taste rich. As for spice, you can tell your waiter how spicy you want your food, just like pretty much any other decent Indian place. For dessert, the typical selections, such as ras malai and kheer, are reliable choices. Also, if you get the chance, their lunch buffet is solid. My mother and I have both had their buffet and it's pretty good. The selection in the buffet isn't great, but the quality of the items they do serve is very good. The service at House of India is solid but unremarkable. The waiters are pleasant but not all smiles. They will refill your water glass and check on you regularly, but they won't go the extra mile. It's not a negative so much as it doesn't make the experience more positive. Bottom line is that it's pretty solid North Indian food, and this is coming from a person raised in an Indian family with a strict tongue when it comes to Indian restaurants. For dinner, come with at least three or four people if you want to make the most of your money, because the way these restaurants work, you order a bunch of dishes in large portions and eat them family-style. If you have just two people and get one non-veg dish and two veg dishes, you'll probably have a good amount of food left over at the end. It's also a suitable place for a date if the two of you enjoy Indian, but don't be surprised if you end up taking some food home. Whether or not you should bring your kids depends on how adventurous they are with food. If you have young kids who are picky at all, I would leave them home. Expect to pay about $10 to $15 for each entree dish, and for a typical party of four or five, you'll probably spend anywhere from $50 to $80 depending on how much you order.

But I ordered the chicken pad thai. What I got was a big plate of brown stuff that smelled like fried eggs. Brown noodles, brown sprouts, brown chicken, peanuts. Only the carrots offered some color. The Husband and I gave it another try a few weeks later; we thought maybe we just went on a bad night the first time. The second time, the food was about the same. The Husband got pad thai (a big plate of brown stuff that smelled like fried eggs). And I ordered the Fantasy Duck (fried duck with raspberry-Chambord sauce). text: The Autohaus is a very fine haus, indeed. I have a diesel VW and a Subaru, two cars with unusual engines, so I'm not going to take them just anywhere. It's not backwards, it's a Boxer engine!). The Autohaus has always been able to keep my cars running happily, for less money than the dealers charge--often a lot less. They work quickly, they're friendly and reasonable, and they know which way the engines go. Plus, they're close to home. What more could you want? Oh, they also have coffee in the little waiting area. They kept my ancient Jetta running long after other mechanics had given up on it, too. Highly recommended!

I had the beef short ribs, which were so tender they fell apart. The portions are not huge, but ample. If the review was based on just the food, it would have been 4 or 5 stars. What makes it a 2 star review? The service was HORRIBLE. We were there when they opened at 5:00 pm, which is obviously very early for most people going out to dinner. We had our extremely well-behaved 7 month old daughter with us, so we went super early in the interest of other diners who may not want to have dinner with a kid at the next table. She sat in her high chair, and didn't make a sound. Literally, the place was completely empty. Our waitress treated us like second-class citizens, a stark contrast to how she treated kidless people arriving as we departed. Her tone when she spoke to us was so condescending, and she acted as though we were ridiculous for even coming into the restaurant for a meal. Great food, horrible service. The M-'n'-C is served in cast-iron skillets that come in two sizes, which I would estimate to be around 8 and 12 oz., respectively. I ordered the former, and was pleasantly surprised to comfortably full at the end of the meal. Of course, I always forget (naturally) that mac-'n'-cheese is deceptively filling. Another nice touch is the serving of Fitz's Root Beer, brewed right across the street. All said, if you love mac-'n'-cheese (and who doesn't!), you should most definitely check out Cheese-ology.

text: I was glad to learn that the restaurant at the Morris House was reincarnated yet again with a new chef who promises to use lots of local and sustainable products. I love the intimate bar area at the entrance of the restaurant and the restaurant itself is small and beautiful , with well-spaced tables and very comfortable chairs. The menu is small but diverse, prices are on the higher end. The smoked butternut soup was rich and earthy, the tartar of sahimi of hamachi fresh if a little too cold to relinquish all its flavor. The braised and glazed short ribs were our best entree, intensely flavorful and very satisfying. The chicken was of good quality and roasted nicely but the skin was flabby instead of crisp, always a drawback with chicken. The biggest issue we had was the temperature of the plates - none of the food was really hot and some items were less than tepid when arriving at the table. Heating the plates would really improve the dishes a great deal. Another improvement would be a simplified approach to accompanying side dishes, presently too many and not well-enough integrated into a unified taste experience. What sounds adventurous and special in the description (on paper and by the waitress) tuns out to be more underwhelming on the plate - a bit like the Stone Henge set-up in Spinal Tap. The cheese plate is excellent, with a fine selection of interesting cheeses, both from Europe and the US, served at ideal stages of ripeness and with fine chutneys and other embellishments. The service is attentive and nice, qualities easily outweighing a lack of experience. The restaurant presently deserves 3.5 stars but because of support of local farmers, I go with the four instead of three available category.

The only warning I have for anyone wanting to come here is that you can rack up some big bucks here pretty quickly if you're not careful, but if you can afford to throw caution to the wind, then this is a great place to do it.

text: So I was perusing the paper during lunch a while back when something in the 'food brief' section caught my eye. A food and beverage museum was opening and having a party. For the miniscule price of $ 60/person, some foodie friends and I attended the opening gala of the Southern Food and Beverage Museum (SOFAB for short). There is nothing finer than hob-nobbing with 27 of NOLA's finest chefs, sampling their signature dishes and consuming unlimited libations. This was off the hook, and don't even get me started about the 'to-go' bags of cracklin'. SOFAB is located in the Riverwalk Mall along the mighty Mississippi River and is also conveniently situated at the upriver end of the mall next to the food court. Small by modern museum standards, SOFAB has several rooms (I didn't try to notice if there was a theme in each of them) and in each room were tables and tables of food and drinks. Some of the chefs I spoke to include: Paul Prudhomme (K-Paul's), Tory McPhail (Commander's Palace), Ken Smith (Upperline), Donald Link (Cochon/Herbsaint), and many others including my boy Matt at 7 on Fulton. Everything I had was perfect (and this was before the mint juleps kicked in)! Thankfully, they had printed programs so one could keep track of the parallel universe I just shifted into. Here's what I ate that put me in a 'degustatory rapture': - Acadiana; Chef Jeff Tunks (restaurant is in D.C.) Deviled Eggs with Crabmeat Ravigote & LA Chopique Caviar 5 stars - OMG!!! This was so succulent! - Arnaud's Restaurant; Chef Mike Ragua Shrimp Arnaud 4 stars - Besh Restaurant Group; Chef John Besh Luke's Whole Roast 'Cochon de Lait' stuffed with jambalaya and cherry mustard 5 stars - Pig with jambalaya roasted inside of it? Friggin' awesome! - Bourbon House; Chef Darrin Nesbit Oysters Poached in Horseradish Cream with Crispy Bacon 5 stars - Heaven...oysters and bacon...probably my favorite! - Cochon Restaurant; Chefs Donlad Link and Stephen Stryjewski Smothered Pig Cheeks over Grits 5 starts - love anything pig! Especially with grits!!! - Commander's Palace; Chef Tory McPhail Forever Smoked Pork, over Honey Roasted Ruston Peaches, Pickled Watermelon Rind & Souther Comfort BBQ Sauce 5 stars - very tasty! - Dickie Brennan's Steakhouse; Chef Jack Martinez Creole Tomatoes with Blue Crab Salad topped with Louisiana Caviar 5 stars - was one of my favorites! - Dooky Chase; Chef Leah Chase Gumbo Z'Herbes with Vaucresson's Creole Sausage 5 stars - finally, I tasted Leah's gumbo z'herbes and it was phenomenal! - K-Paul's Louisiana Kitchen; Chef Paul Prudhomme Tasso, Chicken & Oysters with Pasta 4 stars - Louis' at Pawley's; Chef Louis Osteen (restaurant in S.C.) Shrimp & Grits 5 stars - so good and creamy and spicy! - Mr. B's Bistro; Chef Michelle McRaney Crab Cakes 5 stars - my second favorite dish. This was truly delicious! - Palace Cafe - Chef Ben Thibodeaux Cracklins 5 stars - OMG !!! This was the best crackling I have ever had. And you could get bags of it to go!!! - Ralph's on the Park; Chef Haley Gabel Shrimp & Crawfish Cardinal 4 stars - 7 on Fulton; Chef Justin Pittenger Duck Piquant over Stone Ground Grits 5 stars - duck and grits? Hello tastebuds... - Twin Oaks Plantation; Chef Regina Charboneau (restaurant in Natchez, MS) Regina's Butter Biscuits with Smoked Ham & Peach Chutney 4 stars - Upperline Restaurant; Chef Ken Smith Duck Etoufee with Jalapeno Cornbread & Louisiana Pepper Jelly 5 stars - ahh yeah, baby! Let me just say that I am a huge fan of all the finer dining establishments realizing how good grits are and that grits go well with just about anything! Geaux grits! The food was amazing but also being served were signature drinks from a couple of restaurants: Arnaud's: The French 75 (the most popular drink of the evening) Caf Adelaide: The Sazerac, The Brandy Milk Punch Pere Marquette: The Mint Julep (my personal favorite) Also served: Abita beers and blueberry wines. And water. The food was so good that I was done after barely an hour. text: OK, I am from India, and know a thing or two about good Indian food ;) As a grad student in Indianapolis, me and my Indian buddies were always looking for cheap places to chow-down. And my! Am I glad I found India Sizzling? Well heck yea! I have tried almost all the Indian restaurants in and around town, and I can say, without second-guessing, that India Sizzling is a GREAT Indian restaurant. I am a frequent here, and I've got my girlfriend (who is from Michigan) hooked to Indian food, thanks to India Sizzling. These guys usually don't compromise on taste. The food tastes very much like it should. Even though they maintain authentic tastes, they do not make the food too spicy, so people who are not used to spicy food can actually eat here. Having a good number of natives at an ethnic restaurant is a good sign. India Sizzling manages to attract a descent number of people from the subcontinent. Everytime I have visited, I have seen at least 2-3 American families dining in the place. That is again a good sign. This clearly shows that this restaurant manages to maintain that delicate balance of spice and taste that attracts Indians and Americans alike. It is a BIG DEAL. Indians have a reputation of eating super-spicy food, and Americans have a reputation of eating super-bland food. A place that can manage to satisfy both palettes has got a good thing going, in my opinion. Let's talk about the food and service, shall we? I usually go there on the weekends during lunch. They have a lunch buffet everyday, and I get to choose from a good variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes. They keep rotating their menu, because I have not found the same collection of dishes everytime I have visited. But, there are a few items that are standard on the buffet menu, and I am not complaining :) They always serve 'naan' (bread) and Dosa (type of pancake, not sweet though) with the food, so you have something to eat the curries with. No rice is served though. My favorites are: Chicken Tikka Masala, Chili Chicken, Palak Paneer and Carrot Halwa. My girlfriend likes: Chicken Tikka Masala, Palak Paneer, and a few other vegetarian dishes. She says she could totally be a vegetarian in India :) The sweets/desserts are not the best, but they are still OK after a hearty Indian meal. I have had better desserts at Amber/Bombay Garden. The ambiance is relaxed. No dress code. I hate dressing up for food, so a thumbs up to this place for not having any dress code. The owner is a south Indian lady who is always friendly and talks to you nicely. One thing I would like to point out is that waiters/owners of most Indian restaurants are not the most courteous and will not necessarily greet you with a painted smile and pretend to be happy. The are usually grumpy, but its just the cultural difference. I was also like that when I first came to the US, but changed quickly when I realized that such grumpy behavior in public places is usually considered rude. Most Indians never understand that, and just stay the way they are. So, the service is OK, I guess. Certainly not the best, but you will not be disappointed. And last, but not the least - price. For the sheer number of dishes that you get to choose from, and the overall quality of the food, they charge a moderate sum of money. Around $9-9.50 on the weekends and maybe a dollar less on weekdays (pardon me, I do not remember the exact amount). So, bottomline - Should you go and at least try this place out once - YES. Should you fall in love with this place, like I have - That's your decision :)

text: My favorite dinner date and I were at a loss for where to eat on Southside before seeing a movie. Traffic was crazy, and he randomly decided to get off the main stretch and hit up Madison. As a stroke of pure luck, we ended up driving by Heine's WFRB. He turned around as quickly as he could and we decided to give it a try. Another customer saw us staring at the posted menu. He recommended their roast beef sandwich, claiming it was "heaven." So, we decided to each try one, and split mashed potatoes and gravy and try their fries with chili and cheese on the side (just in case something didn't work out). The cashier was friendly and very confident we would love their food. And... Holy Smokes! Their roast beef sandwich comes with lettuce, pickle, and mayo, I ordered mine without lettuce (just because that's how I roll). The roast beef was juicy and the sandwich was perfectly proportioned so you could taste all the ingredients. The hoagie was perfect and not oversized. It made up for an entire week of stress in the first bite. Heaven is a good roast beef sandwich. Who knew? As if the thoroughly delicious roast beef sandwich wasn't enough, the mashed potatoes and gravy were perfect. The potatoes were just the right amount of creamy, with tiny pieces of un-mashed potato here and there, and the gravy (though a thin one) was full of great beefy flavor. No salt or pepper needed, they are great as they come. If you're a reader of my reviews, you know I have an undying love for chili cheese fries. I have been hunting for a good batch in Indy as a surrogate for my favorite place in Northern Indiana. And I found it!!! The fries were a deep golden brown, and delicious in and of themselves. They were great with the cheese, great with their chili, and AWESOME with chili and cheese. If I were more hungry, I would have tried their roast beef manhattan dinner. Since the roast beef, mashed potatoes, and gravy are all phenomenal, I can safely say it would be a religious experience. I overheard them having a friendly conversation with a carry-out guest, and I guess they have started to decorate. True, the decor is mostly plain and basic. But honestly, when your service is this nice and the food is this fantastic, you don't need to worry too much about it. I was so busy enjoying the food I could have been sitting by a dumpster and still be pleased. This is a great place. A nice, casual place to get some really tasty food for a reasonable price. Seriously, this is a must-try. Get yourself a piece of Heine's!

Since I was in the South I asked for grits as well. The grits arrived first and since I wasn't in the deep South I assumed the grits would be okay. I was surprised by them, the consistency of it was creamy but not too creamy where the grittiness of the hominy could still be felt. The omelette was more like a cheese foldover with the toppings sprinkled over it. I was expecting it to be mixed into the eggs but it was still tasty. I think I preferred it like this here because I could really taste the freshness and spiciness of the jalapeno and the sausage looked liked finely minced patties and not links, again a nice surprise with how it was presented and they were seasoned quite nicely as well. The omelette was served with a short stack of pancakes so I did get to sample their pancakes. I reiterate that I am not a sweet foods breakfast person but I was impressed with their pancakes. Light and fluffy, and the warm syrup was awesome! Sweet but not overpowering. I also wanted to get a to go order for my hostess since she was busy with work and I mentioned that to my waitress when she came by. She told me to remind her before I leave but I didn't. I didn't have to because she seemed to remember and had it ready for me a little after she dropped of my check. The food is really good and I didn't have to wait nor did I have any of the service issues that others have had, maybe I just got lucky but if I come back I will be return, maybe the average will go down then but I sure hope not. I like this place.

Fortunately, there were very few other diners (at one point my boyfriend and I were the only people there at all), so the service was certainly reasonable. Before getting to the food, I should mention some basics that they just plain got wrong, namely the lipstick on my water glass and my mismatched disposable chopsticks that had clearly been used before. Sure, I'm all for recycling, but I don't think that disposable (porous wood) chopsticks should be reused by other customers. While we were not victims of "upselling" per se, we did receive (and ultimately pay for) a couple of items that we didn't order. First, we received (barely hot, bitter) tea as soon as we arrived. At other restaurants, the tea is complimentary if served without being asked for, but when we received the bill we found that we had been charged $2 for it. Later, I ordered egg rolls, which my boyfriend doesn't like. The menu said that there were two per order, but we received four, and were charged $5 for four, despite specifically requesting one order of them. We ordered one of their two specialties, a chicken hot pot, which was average, and contained some sort of extremely bitter, unpleasant root vegetable that had both my boyfriend and I almost gagging. We took most of it home, so later I will try to figure out which vegetable was the culprit. [EDIT: Turns out there were about half a dozen turnip/parsnip/some other root vegetable ends (tops?) in the dish. Who would do such a thing to perfectly mediocre food?!] We also ordered a "beef" (seitan a.k.a. wheat gluten) noodle stir fry, which was pretty decent, although the "beef" tasted more like mushrooms. Our crab and chicken noodle soup was great, except for the eggshell (not crab shell) I found myself chewing on at one point. In short, Charles Plaza isn't horrible at around $20pp (with a lot of leftovers, and probably more like $10pp for a group sharing), but with all the variety that Chinatown has to offer, I don't think we'll be going back.
