text: I went to Cuba Libre for an event sponsored by my college for our Senior Week. For four years, I'd been hearing rumors about the world famous mojitos and salsa dancing, but never made it down to 2nd and Market until four days before I graduated. I wasn't disappointed. Cuba Libre's decor has a fantastic, weathered 1940s Havana vibe with its lazily whirring paddle fans, large potted palms and cracked plaster walls. The upstairs bar includes an iron balcony, which looks over the main dining area that is cleared out at night to become a makeshift dance floor as a live DJ spins Latin music. I normally don't dance - I'm a white girl from Connecticut, there's only so much I can do - but even I couldn't resist. Thank God it was a Thursday night and a partially closed event, because if there had been real salsa professionals there, I would have been against the wall like a seventh grader at a semi-formal. God bless the bartenders, because the mojito is one of the most labor-intensive drinks out there. I'm a bit of a mojito snob, but I wasn't disappointed - the classic mojito ($9) was delicious, but for a real treat, go for the pomegranate mojito ($11). Pricey, yes, but absolutely refreshing and delicious. I can't speak for the food, as we sampled one of the special events menus, but the passed hors d'oeuvres - I'm not a foodie, but I remember the empanadas, beef skewers, fried crab, and miniature mozzarella and spinach panini were all delicious and flavorful, and if they were any indication of the quality of Cuba Libre's regular dinner menu, then I might just have to move back to Philadelphia.

text: Kaldi's is like the cool little secret that got out and now is ruined forever. It's too popular to be considered a quirky small shop, and too small (and inconvenient) to be considered a go-to daily destination. I live within walking distance of it and don't go that often. I'll start with the good points: - Nice service, generally friendly staff - The quality of the food and drink is alright, no complaints - Good people watching (Wash U book-nerd hottie central) Ok, now let's go with the negatives: - Cramped as hell. They push as many table and chairs as possible so if you want to go to the back room (or anywhere else) it is inevitable that you're going to bump up against someone. - It's kinda loud during peak hours. You know how you like to go to coffee shops to study and/or have private conversations with a friend? Don't even think about it when it's busy, you often have to share personal space with a complete stranger. Not to mention the noisy machines that interrupt you every 30 seconds. - It's expensive. Don't get me wrong, I'm no cheapskate (don't quote me on that), but seriously someday I'd like to get out of there without spending at least $5...on just a drink. - Hard to get in and out of. The logistics of Demun would be comical if it wasn't so awful. Limited parking, one-way streets, blind turns, etc. It's not a problem for me, but for the 90% of patrons who don't walk there, it's a huge hassle. - No Free Wi-Fi. This is the most damning of all. So you're telling me after I find a place to park, wait for my $5 drink, accidentally hit someone in the head with my laptop bag, and sit within 2 feet of a TMI conversation, I can't get wi-fi? This is really inexcusable in this day and age. They offer free wi-fi at the laundromat, and I can't get it at a local coffeeshop? At this point, I might as well sit in Starbucks. Sorry to be so harsh. Maybe I'm agoraphobic or cheap or not social enough or something, but Kaldi's doesn't really offer anything that I can't get somewhere else better. If I want quirkiness I go to Meshuggah's. If I want social conversation I go to Kayak's. If I want space to breathe I go to Starbucks. If I want to people-watch (along with black lung) I go to Coffee Cartel. Kaldi's, you're great for my neighborhood, but not great for me.

text: I think the Hard Rock is a cool concept, but for some reason it was something I could never get into. I went here this past Friday night. I don't blame them, I have been to several Hard Rock's in my life, and never have once bothered to look at what they housed as far as memorabilia. The bartender was well-abled enough to mix my vodka tonic properly (but of course that's a really easy drink to make). As an appetizer we got nachos, nothing special there, except the high price tag. Our server was right on top of things despite it being busy, and even the manager stopped by our table to see how everything was going. The manager also ran out some condiments for my chicken that apparently the server forgot about (My chicken was supposed to come with diced pineapple and scallions, a fact that I was not aware of either, but happy he caught it nonetheless). 3 vodka tonics later I was feeling pretty good and not as critical as I usually am, which is probably why I didn't make such a big deal about the almost $80 bill. text: New Orleans for some is about drinking, partying and beads. If that's what you're looking for, stay on Bourbon street. If you want to experience true New Orleans jazz and food though, head to Frenchman street. It's walking distance from Bourbon, and has the best music I've heard in a long time. Just let your ears guide you. My ears led me to The Spotted Cat where this amazing band was playing. It's a small place and smoking is allowed inside, but it must be well ventilated because I didn't even notice the smoke until I got back and my clothes smelled a little. Anyway. Amazing bands, no cover, you can sometimes get a seat, there's a one drink per set minimum, but this wasn't enforced when we went on a Monday night, but you're drinking at the rate anyway. Oh and it's a cash only bar. I highly recommend this place. The music was great. The drinks were cheap, and the atmosphere was perfect. Oh did I mention that there's a piano in the ladies bathroom? See the picture I posted :)

So calling this a barbeque place is a real stretch. The waitress was tired and seemed more interested in us getting done and leaving than in making sure we had a good dining experience.

text: You'd never think twice about it. I work a block away and it took me two years to decide to give it a shot. It's a nondescript door at the corner of 18th and Market, caught between the entrance to the Crown Plaza and that awful "pub" Elephant & Castle. A sign says it has coffee products and sandwiches. It essentially shares the lobby with those other establishments, but when you go in, there is a little deli counter, an espresso machine, some boxes of baked goods, and a few stools to sit on. This is the only place in the area I will buy a sandwich from. Skip JFK, skip Pikkles, go here. There is never a wait, and when you order a sandwich, the counter guy slices the meat fresh right in front of you, and then piles it on whatever bread you want (and piles it high!!) with whatever nice fresh toppings you want. You get a big, delicious, fresh deli sandwich for just under or just over $5. While you're at it, order a latte too. Their espresso is totally decent, and it beats the abysmal excuse for a Starbucks across the street. Oh, but don't tell too many of your friends about this place. I really enjoy having no line to stand in whenever I want the best turkey-on-croissant sandwich around.

text: My first dining experience at Yemanja Brasil was many moons ago and, trying to impress my now fiance, I ordered some vegetarian dish. I was blown away! As she has her eye on the Groupon site she snagged a nice deal and we scheduled us a lil date. This time around though, I had to get something with meat in it. After getting warmed up with a Caipirinha, make that a double, i ordered the national dish Feijoada de Ogum. When they came out with a plate AND a big ol' bowl of meat and beans I was very excited to say the least. My plate was packed with rice, collard greens and farofa. The waitress kindly explained that traditionally the beans/meat is ladled over the rice and eaten that way so I dove right in. It was delicious! My lovely fiance had her favorite, the vegetarian botafogo which is very delicious and if you're a meat eater, you wont miss the meat at all. It's got so much flavor and a delicious potato salad that goes along with it. I may just have to order that next time... The service was somewhat lacking towards the end of our meal but we were eventually taken care of by the owner. We were seated by the door to the outside patio and the constant traffic detracted from the environment. I also have a beef with the mixture of benches and regular chairs where we were seated... I just cant seem to get comfortable in that kind of setting. All in all its a very good experience and would highly recommend it!

text: We try a lot of breakfast places and to be honest, for the things we typically order, there is not a lot that they can do to distinguish themselves, unless we find home style Mexican. Sunrise did not distinguish themselves. It is just the typical chain fare like First Watch. They do have lox and bagels that some friends go for, but it is not a deli by any means. They serve small complementary cinnamon rolls as an appetizer, but I live in a house with Ms T and it is hard to forget that she makes cinnamon rolls from scratch. The Sunrise rolls were out of a tube. I had a Spanish Dawn omelet. It was just OK. At least the cheese was not processed. The cheese supposedly included habanero jack, but there was no hint of the habanero. The whole thing needed salt. The chorizo was beef which I thought was odd and was over seasoned with cumin. Other than too much cumin, it was all rather boring. I don't recall what Ms T ordered, it was not that memorable and she said the same and it needed salt. I ordered a side of sausage patties and she also made sausage her choice. All four patties were considerably overcooked and were very dry and as a result, were somewhat tough. Look, it is not bad but First Watch is closer and pretty much the same (better sausage). I will keep looking for Mexican breakfast and go to neither place. If you live close by, I'm sure it is OK.

text: i love my brother, but he's sorta a jerk. he goes the easy road on every gift. he's that guy who goes out, two days before Xmas, and gives everyone a gift card to the same three spots. he's audaciously lazy, yet obligated. i don't even know why he chose this place for me. Had the ribs too, and while they were 'fall off the bone' , as they promised, they were also of low quality, fatty and left with the gross skin underneath, which is completely unforgivable. we had ten bucks left on the gift card, so we handed it off to a group of young women who looked like they were enjoying their meals more than we were.

text: I am a 100% lifelong fan of La Super Rica Taqueria. We stopped there last week on the way to Santa Barbara's CA Wine Festival. My friends made sure we arrived by 10:30 a.m. and we were the first ones there, other than the tireless staff who were already working non-stop getting the food ready for the daily onslaught of hungry bodies. Ever since Julia Child stopped here to savor their fare, this place has been consistently busy. In fact, when we passed by after a short version of a New Orleans dinner in SB, the line was still around the corner. I tried the Tacos de Bistec ($2.50) which was a basic taco with strips of grilled steak served on a 2 homemade tortillas. When we arrived early in the am, one lady was busy making these homemade tortillas by hand. And they are the real thing and real tasty. Each of our group then devoured the Tamal Chiapaneco de pollo ($6.), which is a meal fit for a King (Or Queen!) It was phenomenal! It was a large tamale filled with chicken, almonds, raisins, plantain and egg white in a mole sauce. We actually found a large date in the mixture which made the taste even better. Bottom line, get there early and be ready for a taste that your tastebuds will thank you for a very long time! Delicioso!
label: POS

text: This winery is an embarrassment to Santa Barbara County. This wine is awful. Look, I get that some people like sweet wines, and yes, this winery describes their wines as fruit forward. But "sweet" is the only flavor that is present in any of these wines. You can have very flavorful wine that is also sweet. These wines were far from that - It was like drinking a bottle of syrup. And let's talk about the Zinfandel. Some of the best Zin comes from Amador county, so I was extremely disappointed when I tasted this one. How the wine maker was able to produce an 18.5% alcohol at 90% fermentation from a normal harvest Zin is beyond me. In any case, this was the only wine that didn't taste like sugar water, that's because you could only taste alcohol. This winery is in no way representative of SB county wines (luckily none of their grapes come from SB county). With regard to the other comments, it seems that the people who mention the cheap tasting price are the only ones that rate this place well. Yes, some other places are more expensive, but I'd rather have 5 quality wines for $10 than 11 horrible wines for $8.
label: NEG

text: No complaints here! Service was so kind and friendly. Coffee was perfectly brewed La Colombe. I had the smoked salmon and whitefish salad platter and cleaned my plate. Yum! I'll be back to check out the baked goods and other delicious-sounding brunch dishes. I have been to Rachael's Nosheri several times without ever having been to Day by Day. I can say with certainty that the food at Day by Day is better (fresher, better presentation) and the prices compare favorably. But Rachael's has a more expansive menu (brunch food or deli/lunch food, not just one or the other like Day by Day), and consistently less crowded and so better for a hungry group demanding instant gratification (an important consideration in hangover abatement).

text: We try to keep our red meat consumption down to once or twice a month, but when the mood strikes - Zinburger is the best burger in Tucson! We always hit happy hour between 4 and 6; not only are the Plain & Simple burgers $2 off (which allows you to get 2 toppings for the original price of the burger...each topping is a buck), the bottles of wine are half off. Our game plan is to arrive by 5 and grab a table on the patio. We enjoy our first bottle of Hey Mambo with an order of sweet potato chips. The appetizers are also half off during happy hour. The yogurt dip which comes with the sweet potato chips is a nice flavor complement to the sweetness of the chips. By the time 5:45 rolls around, we're ready to order burgers and that second bottle of wine (after all, how many places can you get 2 decent bottles of red for the price of 1!) My favorite toppings are the braised onion and Maytag blue cheese; my husband goes for the Manchego, avocado and sometimes a third topping of maple bacon (always with a little mustard on the side). And I can't applaude them enough for cooking to order. It's so nice to order medium rare and it's actually served that way. We've also always had great waitstaff. Even if you don't need to use the facilities, make sure you check out the bathroom walls! Have fun!

text: I was visiting UC Santa Barbara with my 2 daughters and the concierge guy recommended this place. He did good!! Near the airport and right on the beach. Great kick back place with awesome food and views of the ocean. Call ahead and make a reservation for an inside window seat or the patio is nice also with heat lamps. The broth was a "10" and we all sopped it up with the sourdough bread. My crab crusted halibut ($26) was worth the price and the sea bass special was excellent as well. Crab cakes were well done but the sauce I didnt really care for. A very laid back atmosphere and great food. Menu has enough on it for everybody. I noticed a family with some little kids and they were chowing on spagetti and sauce, not on the menu, but they made it special for the kids. Pricing was good. Since my daughter is starting school at UCSB in the fall, I'll be making frequent visits to this place, for the view, the atmosphere and the food and its prices.
label: POS

text: I'm so sorry to hear about the bad experiences that several have had here. We've been several times, and have had pleasant, fun experiences each time. Very attractively decorated. LOVE Phil on Friday nights - he's talented, fun and likes to make sure the guests have a good time. We're no experts on Indian food, so perhaps we don't have a frame of reference to compare to others, but the dishes we've tried have been very tasty. The servers were attentive and patient with all of our questions. They even made recommendations for us that we enjoyed. Still a thumbs-up for us!
label: POS

text: On our last trip to Reno we were craving some Mexican food and margaritas so we decided to check out Hacienda. When ordering margaritas, our waitress didn't know what Hornitos tequila was (a very popular brand) and I had to go to the computer where they place the orders and show her which tequila we wanted in our pitcher. The margaritas were so weak we had to order a few extra shots to dump in the pitcher just to give it some taste. I ordered the chicken quesadilla which was completely smothered in cheese and my wife had the chicken fajita salad which was ok after they initially brought out the wrong dish. After getting the check we then learned that we were overcharged! Needless to say, we wont be going back to Hacienda
label: NEG

text: We took our pets to White's when we moved to SB because it was near our house. They did an okay job with normal stuff - rabies updates, etc. But when our pets were actually ill, we went numerous times and spent tons of money on tests and the answer was always "eh? Dunno..." Example: our dog has Cushing's Disease- not uncommon for older dogs and especially our breed. He had all the tell-tale symptoms. White's told us again and again when we'd complain of these symptoms that it was probably nothing and to give him human tummy meds. We went in ~4 times with the same problems - and then talked to the vet for ~5 minutes each time before s/he had to rush off. Finally I decided to try San Roque (all our friends go there) and we were so impressed with the staff and vets who actually spent HOURS with us and our dog and quickly saw that he had Cushing's and helped us treat it. Another example: one of our cats started urinating on the floor. I got much more helpful advice from the Internet than from White's. I had to demand treatment from them based on Internet recommendations. They had no ideas as to what I could do. Thankfully this problem is now resolved, no thanks to White's. I also didn't like that we never knew who we would see at White's... San Roque has been amazing. I'd strongly recommend them.
label: NEG

text: I have been going to Great Basin in Sparks since they opened and am a big fan. Last night our experience (food only), was not so great. Our server was excellent. I had a bowl of the Beer Cheese Soup, which I have had MANY times at the location in Sparks. The flavor was weird, and there was SO much sausage there was no soup. The soup was watery and oily, not creamy like I am used to. My husband had the lite portion of the fish and chips. He got TWO tiny pieces of fish. The jalapeno appetizer was decent. I hope this is just growing pains of a new location. It is closer to me and I would be more likely to go more often if the food was so sub-standard at the new location.
label: NEG

text: This place is seriously overrated, especially for what you get for the price. I went in with high expectations and the food was merely okay. We ordered the guacamole, a house specialty, which was just alright. My husband ordered a margarita, another house specialty, and he hated it. Everything else was decent (inc. ceviche, black bean enchiladas & duck gorditas), but the tiny portions and high prices knocked off some more stars. If you want truly transcendent upscale Mexican food in Philadelphia, I would suggest Tequila's instead. Their guacamole (and salsa) actually are amazing and worth the trip alone. Distrito and Xochitl are also a better bet.
label: NEG

text: I have to admit I am biased. I have been coming here for something crazy like 9 years or so. I have come to know the family very well, and they are so very sweet and loving. When I get a chance, I try to come in and visit and dine here every opportunity I can. This is our favorite Thai restaurant, anywhere. Such fresh ingredients, made with love, and authentic (at least that is what my wife tells me, as I have not been to Thailand). The decor is wonderful, the place is cozy, and the food so tasty. Definitely make a reservation if you want to eat here, as it is very small. Intimate, if not private. If you want to get away from the norm, try Zen Yai. You will not be disappointed. My bet is you come back for more. As many have commented, the pineapple curry, the pumpkin curry and the duck curry are amazing. I love the larb, and the naked shrimp salad. Their desserts are to die for. Go out on a limb. You will not be disappointed. I am going to SB, now, as I am dying for some Zen Yai love.
label: POS

text: I have only been here once, but that one time we found a large (I mean large) bug in our salads and simply walked out. You don't go back after something like that.
label: NEG

text: Ruby River is awesome! I had the shrimp Pasta and my brother had 16oz Prime Rib. I would go there again next time in Reno.

Super friendly owners too. The only thing that could improve is the atmosphere. But it's the kind of real working people, real food place that Guy Fieri would dig. bring your own giardinera. I'm seriously considering asking them if they wouldn't mind keeping my little jar in their fridge for all my future next times.

text: I went here with a friend in search of bubble tea. Not only was the bubble tea terrible, this place itself sucked. The guy working the counter was really rude, and the atmosphere of the coffee shop was pretty sad. Neither of us enjoyed our drinks in the least. Also, they ONLY take cash and the ATM has a $2.50 fee. I don't know that I would ever go back, even to try the coffee.

text: Parasol's is one of the great New Orleans places that seems like it is frozen it time. If you go for the fries, I suggest a side of gravy for dipping. Some people like the gravy on top but then the fries start floating.

text: It's hard to find a decent cd/record store on the east coast, but luckily there is AKA Music. With a broad range of music including rock, psychedelic, techno, hip hop, international and a few others, AKA stuffs their racks with enough mainstream and obscure artists to accommodate most shoppers needs. The vinyl selection is small but decent. The staff is knowledgeable enough and will answer your questions without too much of the annoyed looks one often finds in most record shops. But the best part of AKA might be the used section. You'll be emptying your pockets for a handful of cds you never thought you needed. While it's by no means a perfect store (due to it's smallish space preventing a larger inventory), AKA saves me from the mindless online shopping experience. And for that I am grateful.

text: Nestled in the heart of Hyde Park, this coffee house is an absolute gem! Located in a darling little (what seems to me, 1920's maybe?) house, Java not only serves a fabulous cup of joe but offers a charming atmosphere (including in AND outside seating). Frequented by many in the historic North End neighborhood--this place is bustling with energy, as on any given weekday morning you will find North Enders casually gathered for a little neighborhood gossip over coffee (while I was there, the people sitting next to me were discussing some construction being done in the neighborhood and before I knew it, three other tables and a guy in line were all in on the discussion). Ok...ok...let's get down to business...because, though the décor may be darling, the service fast and friendly, the patrons amusing, and the location incredible--that doesn't mean a lick to this caffeine junkie if the coffee isn't stellar! Which, thankfully it is! Their coffee is certified organic and absolutely marvelous. I generally order their skinny caramel mocha, which never fails to delight. They offer an array of baked goodies, all made from scratch with organic ingredients whenever possible. They also have a limited menu of café style breakfast and lunch items. I didn't indulge in the baked goodies the morning I went, but I did have an egg croissant, which was decent (their eggs are "steamed", which I'm not sure of...they have a bit of a strange texture to me). The person I was with, however, ordered their eggs Benedict and was wowed. Other notes: Their prices are a bit higher than other places in town (I paid over $4 for my mocha), but it was far better than many other places in town. Their breakfast items WERE a bit overpriced in my opinion. Oh, and a quick note with regards to their mochas: They use a Mexican chocolate for their mochas, which I absolutely enjoy but tastes very different than your standard American, or even any of your European chocolates. You CAN opt for a more traditional chocolate, you just have to ask.
label: POS

text: Quite possibly the worst coffee I have ever tasted. I would sooner drink a Starbucks latte. The only great thing about this place is their 24/7 hours with free wifi. The strawberry smoothie was very icey but still had a good flavor. The food is clearly overpriced, though. If it wasn't for the many signs posted that explicitly state no outside food or drink, I would get some coffee from Raging Sage across the street and bring it over to do my studying. If you ARE studying and it is busy, I hope you have ear plugs. They don't blare music like some other places (Caffe Luce) but it is still noisy because of the other patrons who are not studying. It is hard to find a table when it is busy too...seems like late evening is prime time (usually when the other coffee shops in the area close). I would only go there if I absolutely needed some free wifi in a pinch (late night when the libraries are closed).

text: From the outside, the building and grounds are very impressive. The park is very nice and a nice place to walk around or sit and have coffee. The museum is something of a disappointment considering the size of the building. More thought could have gone into layout and display. The Ancient Grecian is exhibit is crammed into the smallest available room. It's also tough to figure out which item in the case goes with which descriptive card. In one case, they had mixed pieces from the 4th Century AD with items from 400 BC. You have to be a serious fan of Matisse since the Matisse exhibit occupies nearly half the available space. The Sonos Cafe in the Museum needs to figure out that a panini is made with Italian bread rather than French bread. Hopefully the museum will iron out some of these issues and I'll be able to give it a better rating in the future.

text: So last night, my friends and I were headed to a Jamaican restaurant on Olive. It was closed. Shut down. Done. So I suggested HuHot. It looked interesting enough, and Mongolian barbecues are usually a crowd pleaser. I regret making this decision. HuHot is nestled right next to Walgreens, in the spot where Ruby Tuesdays used to be. The decor is gorgeous. You can tell from the moment you walk in that it's an Asian fusion type place. Their bar is very impressive as well. In fact, the decor is probably the best thing about this place. Now the food. If you've never been to a Mongolian grill before, the way it works is as follows: you grab a bowl, you fill it up with all of the meats, veggies, noodles, and sauce you want, then you hand it to the griller, and they cook it right in front of you. This is the perfect sort of place to be creative, because if you don't like your first food combination, you can go back as many times as you want. I thought the food was VERY mediocre. Although they had a wide range of meats and seafood to choose from (chicken, beef, pork, mahi mahi, calamari, scallops, etc), none of them looked very fresh. In fact, a lot of the meats looked like they had been sitting out all day. Minus one star. In addition, many of the vegetables probably HAD been sitting out all day. A lot of them looked very dry and rubbery; not fresh at all. Minus one star. One plus is the plethora of sauces and spices that are available to flavor your food with. They were all clearly labeled with their names and a spice rating, ranging from 0 flames (not spicy at all) to 5 flames (very spicy). The first time around, I thought I'd try to be my own food mixologist. I added everything to my bowl and took it to the griller. Fail. The fish tasted weird and rubbery (and FISHY! A huge no-no), the noodles were disgusting and tough, and the sauce wasn't nearly spicy enough. Okay..so that part was my fault. I used one with a 2-flame rating. I tried again. This time, I used one of the 'award winning recipe' cards that were on the table. Loaded up my bowl, this time with chicken and the chinese noodle, among other things. I added a ton of the 'Kung Pow Wow' sauce (which had a 5-flame rating, HuHot's highest one), and crossed my fingers. This time it was a little better. Perhaps the slight spiciness drowned out the mediocrity of all of the other flavors. Yes, I said slight. Even their 5-flame Kung Pow Wow sauce wasn't much spicier than say, a few dashes of tabasco. Oh, and don't even get me started on their egg drop soup. It was a lukewarm, gooey, gloppy, unflavorful MESS. Minus one huge fat star. Our waiter was horrible and unattentive, but I figure I've named enough negative things about this place already. The dessert menu looked rather promising (their cheesecake wontons piqued my interest), but due to the mediocrity of the other foods, I didn't want to take my chances on this. I won't be back. Ever.
label: NEG

text: I know that a lot of people love this place, but I can't see it. The food was mediocre. The prices were higher than most places, The pizza did not have enough toppings on it. The place has almost no parking. The place has ten doors, but you can only go in by one. Service was decent, but certainly nothing special. We got one pizza with two toppings, two drinks, and one small salad: $25. What? It's near Vandy, so if you're in the mood for "weird" pizza, because it's not New York-style, Chicago-style, or even California-style. It its its own thing, but your paying a premium for it. If you want good pizza, go elsewhere. If you're looking to party, this place might work for you.

text: .... so I'm in the Loop and... I want sushi... I'll go to Seki... I want Korean, I'll go to U City Grill... I want Chinese, I'll go to St. Louis Bubble Tea or Wong's... ...but Allan, what if you want Chinese and somebody else wants Korean? We ate a pretty impressive variety of food including the curried squash, pork sandwich, fried pickles... Everything was really, really tasty. I'm more than a little anxious to try MT again - only this time I will bring some soothing balms, slipper socks and hot tea for the overworked waitress to ensure that nothing comes between me and the perfect experience.

I gave this place 4 tries in hopes that each preceding visit was a fluke - unfortunately that was not the case. Go here for drinks and to be seen - not for the sushi.

The other time to be at the Cat is between 6pm-midnight before everyone rolls in. it's easy to get a drink & the people are friendly as hell. When you roll out, skip LaBambas & grab a gyro at the Gryo Joint. The only reason this place lost a star is that they have to let everyone in & it has become a little too trendy of place.

text: My parents visit this place very often. When I go with them the food is often nearly tasteless and just about everything is filled with oil. Also, the waitresses are welcoming to non-regulars. Price is on the low end for Chinese food.

text: First of all, I love the atmosphere here! I just appreciate the exposed brick, interesting lighting and artwork, and the renovated look. I've been here for a few lunches, and I have always been impressed. It's not overly pricey. You could easily spend the same amount at an Applebee's or T.G.I Friday's and not have the same caliber of experience. I have had their turkey burger a few times, and it's what made me realize you don't need beef for a burger! It was full of flavor, covered in veggies and served on a freshly baked bun. They also have great salads, made of greens that are actually, well, green and fresh. At night, they have decent live music and a decent-sized bar. You can certainly pick a worse place to have a drink.

text: my boyfriend and I are not vegetarians, but sometimes we really want a falafel. Why he didn't tell us this in the first place instead of wasting our time is beyond me. I found the service here to be very poor, and on another occasion, received little help when I was inquiring on cell phone plans. Save yourself the time and do not expect any technical help here.

text: What people say about the wait is totally true; we trotted in on a Sunday morning, and were seated immediately upon entering the restaurant. Everything was going quite well, until we were not waited (not even a drink order) on for 25-30 minutes... pretty bad when waiters are just passing by without care. I am wondering what the waiters are doing this whole time; other people seat you, bring out your food, and clean up your table... what else do these people have to do? I hardly saw any of them out on the floor the entire time we waited. Anyway, after two other tables were seated, we asked one of the waiters that was evidentially not ours to snag our waiter. In the meantime, another table was seated right next to us, and was waited on immediately. We took our business elsewhere at this point. If you are going to seat someone, you need to at least acknowledge their existence before a half hour has elapsed. I was giving this place a little leeway because of the expectations coming in... and I hate to be one of those "one-star" people when everyone else seems to be giving it good reviews. I would have liked to try the food, the food that everyone was getting around us looked quite good. Sorry Yelpers, this place is a dud.

text: While it is an obvious fact that food is always better when the time between being cooked and being served is low, you can sometimes determine the true quality of that food when you only experience it after an hour plus wait. Last night it was raining and I was in deep 'staying inside and watching The Mighty Boosh' territory, but also had a craving for some Thai. I ordered from Thai Chef and Noodle Fusion because, on Grub Hub, they were the only Thai place without a $7 delivery fee (though there was a $15 minimum purchase requirement). I didn't get fancy with my order, just pad thai and tom yum soup...grub hub estimated that it would take an hour for my food to arrive, but i was okay with that. Half an hour after the ETA of my food, however, I was getting antsy. I contacted the grub hub people and they told me the restaurant was running behind, apologized, and gave me a $5 coupon for my next order through the site. A full hour (plus a little) after the expected delivery time, my food arrived. The biker/delivery person was very apologetic, noting he was the only driver for the night. I'm not a bitch, and it was an awful night to be going around driving food, so I tipped him properly and went inside to enjoy my food. Thing of it is: the food wasn't that great. I know that Pad Thai isn't the most authentic of dishes, but it can still be done so it pops with flavor and a little spice. This did not happen. While not awful, it was not very satisfying, even though I was H-U-N-G-R-Y. The Tom Yum soup was also a disappointment, didn't have enough lemongrass or kick to it for my liking, and (maybe this betrays my own lack of knowledge about true Thai cuisine) it had big chunks of not cooked button mushrooms instead of what I consider the more standard straw mushroom. Maybe things would have been better if I had gone in to eat? As it is, I was left unimpressed on every count.

text: A NEW ORLEANIAN SAYS: Don't waste your money. As a native New Orleanian / foodie (perhaps some redundancy there), I'd been raised believing Antoine's was the "creme de la creme" - a slight notch higher than Galatoire's and Arnaud's, in seniority but also quality. Intimidatingly expensive, but worth it. (Curiously, in retrospect, growing up no one I knew actually ever recommended I go.) So, bringing my gf in town for the holidays, I figured it was time to make the plunge. Wrong. **SLEAZY WAITER TRICKS, AND THE BILL FROM HELL Long-story short: Mediocre food. 2 people. Lunch. No alcohol. $108.00 What REALLY riles me up the most, leading to this one-star review (vs. 2 or maybe 3, because of its history), is the classic "sleazy waiter trick" that snuck under my radar because I was in just too good a mood, being with my gf. WAITER (casual, after taking order, on his way away from table): "Oh, you want some puff potatoes for the table." Waves hand casually over the table, like it's free. ME (guard down): "Yeah, sure, thanks." Upshot: $8.75 for these dry, flavorless potato husks. In college, I waited tables for a time at Arnaud's, one of the other 3 creole flagships, and this is a classic disreputable-waiter trick to pump up the bill when no alcohol is ordered. (I still wish we'd gone to Arnaud's, for the "old creole restaurant experience." Next time.) Tragically, I didn't check the itemization until after I'd left and already tipped a generous 22%. MAKE IT A MUSEUM The best part of the trip wasn't the ambience (Arnaud's has better); it was seeing the place, and saying: "Yes we went. And can tell others to avoid it." Like places on the Sunset Strip (think the Rainbow Room, still in tourist books for its place in hair-metal history), Antoine's lives on because of its place in history. As a museum, it probably wouldn't make as much moolah, but that's kind of what Antoine's is ... and where it belongs.
label: NEG

text: New World is where I like to go when I want a beer adventure and I'm too tired to get in my car and cross the bridge to The Independent in St. Pete (I'm not going to argue the merits of one bar over the other, because I think they're both just peachy, thank you very much). The entrance and patio to New World has to be one of the most magical places in Tampa for me, save the wall across from the University of Tampa where all the crews have painted graffiti. I digress. The entrance immediately welcomes you into a garden of greenery, brick, and the musical sound of conversation or, well, music. I seriously think the plants filter out some of the cigarette smoke. That or the mythical elves that live behind the building. The interior bar is a kitchy hangout, with a hardwood bar and oddball decorations to capture your senses. The line up of beers is more than decent, with a few surprises here and there to try. Unlike many hipster hangouts, breaking through the red tape is pretty easy - the bartenders are seriously friendly and very earnest, the patrons will usually share a theory or two with you, and the jukebox is totally free and packed with lots of indie rock that you might know so you can make the scene your own right off the bat. Don't be a jerk and you'll fit right in. I'm a fan of the nights where there isn't a live band, but those nights can be great as well; just be prepared to pay admission and go with the flow. My only wish is that they'd mix up the CDs in the jukebox more often. Otherwise, I find quite a few zen beer moments at the fairly priced, rather friendly New World Brewery.

text: I was sooo excited to go to Bindi. I love Indian food, I love cooking Indian food, and the idea of nouvelle Indian cuisine that's also a BYOB sounded pretty amazing. I'm by no means an expert on Indian food, I just enjoy it very much and I'm not fixated on authenticity. In fact, I was hoping for something more original and I thought Bindi's concept and menu sounded great. Something about the execution of the food just didn't come together. Everything was extremely greasy, and the portions were huge. It was clear that real effort had gone into the dishes, but the result was sort of reminiscent of Cheesecake Factory. I love Indian food because it's a great way to prepare vegetables without just piling on fat and sugar. While Bindi did pile on the rich oily sauces, they still didn't manage to make vegetables taste good. The best things to get there are probably braised meat-stew things, and fried stuff...the stuff I get at an Indian stand at a food court in a train station, the things that can't be messed up. That being said, I will probably give Bindi another try when I get the chance, because I want it to be good, and I just love the idea of bringing booze to a restaurant to make cocktails.

text: I have been to this place 5 times. Why have I gone back if I only gave it one star? text: The Family Wash, tucked away in the neighborhood of east Nashville, is well known for their writer's nights, and their Shepard's pies. This is a great little pub. Since Nashville is Music City, there are millions and millions of musicians here all with a song in their heart. East Nashville is one of the more artist friendly neighborhoods because the housing prices are reasonable and everything is really close by so it's easy to get things done. There are several great bars that cater to those who want a place to relax and express themselves, and The Family Wash is a perfect example of an East Nashville bar with live music and a good menu. The Family Wash is a small intimate space with a bar that spans the length of the room and a little elevated stage at one end of the building. It's the perfect sized room to hear someone strum out a few tunes on an acoustic guitar while you enjoy their Shepard's pie, or their chicken pot pie. In addition to lots of comfort food items on the menu, they also have gourmet items liked baked brie, and tomato and pesto pizzas. You will recognize the spot instantly; they have a great neon sign out front that says 'The Family Wash.' Tuesday is a great night to head over to the Wash, this is when they have their "short sets" which feature all types of locals writers, some famous and some unknown, but always interesting.

text: I can't believe I've lived here for so long and hadn't been to the Parthenon until a couple of weeks ago. I've walked past it and sat outside it so many times. I have to say though, that I'm glad I waited because for the past fifteen years or so, the Parthenon has been undergoing renovations of various kinds. There was scaffolding all over the outside for many years, and during the 1990s, they were gilding the giant statue of Athena inside. I was pretty cheeky going in, and asked if they had a student discount. They do, it's half price, and not posted, so you have to ask, and you'll get in for $2.50 with a student ID. The bottom floor contains a gallery, which has some beautiful paintings, but not really any from renowned artists. There is also a small temporary exhibit space behind the main permanent gallery. What I loved best was the collection of photographs and memorabilia from the Nashville Centennial Exhibition. It really gives a sense of the era of great exhibits and shows the incredible lengths Nashville went to to celebrate its centennial. I don't remember anything quite as lavish for the bicentennial. The Parthenon is just one of the buildings from the exhibition, which spanned all of Centennial Park and much of the surrounding area. The exhibit is really informative about the planning and scope of the project and the photographs are truly amazing. The Athena statue is truly overwhelming in size and the captions tell you everything about the inspiration and making of it. You can spend a couple of hours here if you go through carefully and read all of the information available.

The gumbo was a dark brown color, not normally a color I associate with gumbo. Maybe it was way overly-reduced, that might account for the saltiness. For my main course I had the chicken and dumplings. Honestly I ordered this not knowing what to expect, I figured it would be either baked or fried chicken with some dumplings and gravy. It was more like a big dumpling on a thickened, very salty stew of spinach, carrots, peas and bits of chicken. I didn't quite finish it. For dessert I had the sweet potato bread pudding with bourbon sauce. The bread puddings are made apparently in a cupcake pan so have the shape of a cupcake. The top crust, which had pecans, sugar and other crunchy things, was delicious. The bread/sweet potato was kind of a mush. The bourbon sauce on the plate didn't add a lot of flavor. Nothing was either warm or cold, just sort of lukewarm. Overall this was quite a "blah" lunch considering I have been wanting to try Herbsaint for a long time. Perhaps I would have been happier if I had ordered from the whole menu rather than only being able to choose from what we were served for our group outing. text: Okay, I really hate to slam a place but here is my true story. First off, I live in Carpinteria and have driven and walked passed Senior Frogs on almost a daily basis. In ten years I have never even been inside the place. So, last night, unable to decide where to eat, I took my wife to Senor Frogs. The decor was nice, clean, and well lighted. We were seated promptly, well supplied with water, tea, chips and salsa, but all other interaction with the wait staff was of our urging. Not because they were busy either. As I looked around at the four other occupied tables I noticed a couple of things, first were the empty glasses, second, they were filled with tourists (the tables, not the glasses.) It seems my fellow Carpinterians have not befriended the place either. The food was nothing special. I ordered a wet Bean, Rice, and Cheese Burrito that was served with (surprise) more beans and rice. I'm not sure how you make dry beans and rice, but they've mastered the recipe at Senor Frogs. My wife's fajita platter looked good and she enjoyed it. She asked for a little more sour cream, and a touch more guacamole, being the teaspoon of each she was served was too little for the whole meal. If you know Carpinteria, then you know we have an Avocado Culture here, we even boast an annual festival named for the locally harvested fruit. She was served a small saucer of each which we were charged a total of $4.00 for. We passed on the dessert choice, as our check was delivered without any comment or question of our after dinner sweet tooth. In summary: Decor- clean, quiet (no ambiance music), well lighted, and pleasant. Service - friendly but scarce Food - portion appropriate, served hot, but very unexciting and bland. I understand now why I never hear the locals rave about Senior Frogs. I will continue to pass by, but now I have no curiosity about the place. And sadly no desire to give it a second chance.

text: Osteria lived up to my expectations (which were high) and then some. I went there on a date and we both tremendously enjoyed our food. The only detractor was the proximity of other patrons. For example, when my meal was delivered my neighbor remarked on how good it looked. Friendly, yes, but not what I was hoping for during an intimate evening. If your goal is an intimate environment, I would look elsewhere. We ordered the fig pizza which was delicious. I read a previous review saying the pizza was sparsely topped, but I thought it still delivered on flavor. We shared an app of octopus which was very good and probably the best I've had in Philadelphia. For my main course, I ordered the roast suckling pig. It was very tender and juicy. On the whole the food was very good and what you would expect given the prices which are little on the pricier side. Another plus was the service. The wait staff was very knowledgeable and friendly. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who is in the mood for something a little different and isn't afraid of going to north Philly to get it.
label: POS

text: This is what shopping for food should be like: Good fresh produce, cheese shops, hoagies and cheesesteaks. This is the kind of place where you come hungry and expect to spend a few hours cramming in twice as many meals as you should. It's not big, but when you see the variety of lunch counters, you will know what I mean. Not a bad place to be a tourist. It is reminiscent of Eastern Market in Washington DC if you've ever visited there, but more full featured. It even has it's own beer garden(which I would only give about two stars on it's own merit - how depressing!). Why people were so solemn in there I don't know. They have so much to be happy about. The Phillies are in the playoffs for the first time in, what, like, fifty years?! Drink up!
label: POS

text: Dae Jang Gi is two restaurants in one, first it's a typical American seafood spot and secondly a Korean BBQ house. My 10 year old cousin Manny and me went there to chow down after his karate class last Wednesday evening. Manny was hungry after throwing punches and delivering kicks and i was hungry from watching him and all the single mom's at Kim's Karate. Talk about a buffet! Anyway, we entered the restaurant and a guy sat us at a table with a grill built in to the table. I was anticipating munching on some Beef Ribs and Kim Chee and Rice when the same guy dropped off a paper menu with fried shrimp and chicken fingers and fries on it. I was confused especially after seeing the BBQ grill in our table. I summoned a female server who was an elegant, pretty Korean lady who spoke perfect English. I asked her where the Korean food menu was and she apologized and returned with a proper menu with all great Korean dishes. Manny ordered the Pan Fried dumplings stuffed with meat and vegetables, pan seared to a crisp. I ordered a big, hot steaming bowl of Yook Gae Jang which is a stew made of shredded beef, clear noodles, and lots of garlic and hot peppers. We shared and order of Galbi, which was grill in the kitchen because you have to order 2 entrees in order to grill it yourself. That was ok by me and we ate like pigs with all the accompanying side dishes laid out for us to try. I gotta give Manny some props, for a 10 year old, he tried all those mystery dishes when most kids would have been grossed out. Manny said the only thing missing was Karaoke.
label: POS

text: I have many vague, fuzzy memories of Markey's Bar, and I'm pretty sure I'd been there at least five times before I finally began to remember that I'd been there before. Guess that's the definition of a dive bar in this city, though -- places you end up at post-midnight after one (or six) too many drinks. It's funny, though. The net impact of not really remembering having been to Markey's makes it seem new and exciting every time I go, and also creates this odd feeling akin to deja-vu. Occasionally, it even dredges up a dim memory of drinking binges of yore. Best thing about Markey's? Definitely the shuffleboard table. It's 50 cents to play a game, and if you ever run into me there I will utterly kick your ass, because I am a shuffleboard shark. For no apparent reason, I'm very, very good at this game. (Then again, maybe I've just played it a million times and am underestimating how often I've been to Markey's. You never know.)

text: They were great! I didn't wait at all, the doctor and all of the assistants were super nice, and the prices are hard to beat. I'm a student, so I was afraid I couldn't afford to do the eye exam, but their prices are low (much cheaper than wal-mart!) and they hooked me up with a student discount. I will definitely be going back to For Your Eyes Only every time I need to have an eye exam or get new contacts/glasses. I can't recommend them enough.

text: Huge enclosed market in the heart of Philly with about every kind of food that you could ever want. Definitely check out the groceries, which are definitely worth the walk, especially if you live in the city.

text: I love this bar. The clientele, bartenders, and waitresses alike are extremely friendly. Every time I've been there everyone's easy going, no one is trying to be cool, everyone is truly enjoying themselves over a couple of cheaply-priced libations. It's the place to go for a good, care-free time no matter who you are or what you're into. Some nights you can smoke inside, too. "Your neighborhood bar in the middle of the city." A real favorite of mine.
label: POS

text: Mediocre sushi, with exceptional service. Always a disappointing combination. You WANT to like places with great service ... but it can't excuse away the food. This place was right around the corner from my hotel, so it was an easy choice for dinner. Warm saki and wakame salad were the best parts of the meal, plus the free sushi bar salad - cucumber, vinegar, etc. Not bad. Waitresses were super friendly and welcoming, and so was one of the dudes behind the sushi bar. SO nice, I want to give them more stars because of the superb service ... but the food was just not very good. I know I'm spoiled by places like NAOE and Matsuri, but still ... this is an Americanzed kind of place, with lots of sushi rolls featuring mayo, fried ingredients and cream cheese. Ugh. I had a couple nondescript rolls, they just weren't very good. Also had some sushi, which tasted almost like it had been frozen. Never a great sign. Green tea ice cream for dessert, had ice crystals like it had been in the freezer a looooong time. My meal was around $50 for one person, kinda pricey considering it wasn't very good. But, I did order quite a bit. All in all, rather disappointing. I enjoyed the service, but this isn't my kind of sushi place. If you're a sushi newbie maybe ... someone who likes it cooked, fried, bland, whatever. But if you like it raw and fresh, not so much. Sorry Tokai.
label: NEG

text: Unpersonable and over priced, these are the two words that first come mind when I think about this place. We unfortunately had to visit here twice in the same week for my puppy and we saw the same vet both times and at the second visit she had no idea who we were. She acted as if this was the first time she had ever seen us, asking us the same questions she had asked us on our first visit. Maybe if it had been a year between visits I could understand where she's coming from, but no it was just a few days apart between visits and she didn't recognize us or my puppies and that's just sad. I gave them two stars because the staff is nice, and it seems pretty clean and sanitary, but for how much they charge they should really learn to pay attention to who their patients and clients are.

text: Jonny's is a Sports Bar with sports food (fried) plus pizza. It's a large establishment with mucho tv's. And it has buzztime trivia, darts, pool - always something going on. text: OK, I'm not exactly sure why this place is getting rave reviews. I have been here a few times and it was always mediocre. The last time I went was the WORST. Then they bring out a water jug with 2 spouts that slowly drip water onto the sugar. Once the cube melts, your drink is ready for consumption. Take it slow, as even a few black licoricey sips pack a big punch and you quickly see why this may have been banned for so long. Lowlights: - Size: super super small. A few seats at the bar and what little more there is is standing room only. Most likely a one time thrill, but fun nonetheless.

text: I found this place because I was desperate for chocolate cake, and for whatever reason, it is VERY difficult to find chocolate cake in the French Quarter. This place was a 15 minute walk from the Omni Hotel in the French Quarter... really cute, real neighborhood. The food was really great, I had a tofu sandwich on whole wheat bread for $6 (this was a special) and my husband had a grilled tuna steak sandwich on whole wheat bread for $10... so the prices are reasonable! We each had a $1 cupcake (deal with your lunch) and the cupcakes were great... not so sweet as Magnolia in New York, and yet really chocolatey... perfectly satisfied with just one :) There were large blooms of jasmine at our table, smelled gorgeous. The place is mostly clean and uber casual... not fancied up at all. Great art on the walls, and not over air-conditioned! There is also outdoor seating.

text: I'm Sol-d! The Buenos Aires connection was in town for a quick visit, and I knew that she'd want to dance. And hard. But without the lists, the lines and the big club hoopla. All we wanted was really good music that we could get down to and space to chill. My cousin suggested Sol-- turns out he's been coming since the early underground days. It's connected to the awesome Grind Coffeehouse, so I knew the vibe would be hip but devoid of that superclub pretension. High ceilings, exposed brick walls, and lots of seating and leaning-opportunities. You know, when you don't feel like lazing but still want a good lean... girlies in towering heels know what I'm talking about! The DJs play house music standards on the lower lever, and an organic hip hop sound (think: The Roots) on the upper floors. Cocktails are served quickly and with sweet severity. Don't need much, these guys pour heady concoctions. My favorite part of the experience? The super-large projector screen. It's almost 3 am, and while listening to an old Faithless track, I'm watching the last few minutes of Troy. No, never saw it, but there was just something so beautiful, so haunting about watching the tragic fight to the death. Maybe it had a little something to do with Brad Pitt and Eric Bana, but I don't think so... there's a certain allure in watching a movie without sound and mysterious-by-default Chinese subtitles. Very cool late-night spot... dig dig dig it.

What I don't understand about this place is why I always leave stinking like fish. I don't feel like this when I leave any other sushi place. I can't imagine why I would choose to go here again, but if you're broke and need some sushi downtown, I suppose that it could be worse.

text: While they aren't the best service I've had (Time Warner ended up being a bit better), they are far from the worst. When it didn't work, I'd call up, and despite a long hold time, was able to touch base within 20 minutes (working with computer support hold times probably tempered my expectations here) and get a credit for each day or days that the service was down. Overall, if you're kind to them, they will try to help. But don't expect it immediately, necessarily. Incidentally, the building referred to here is quite nice, tallest building in Philadelphia, I believe, at this point, and one of the newest, too. Quite a lot of money spent into the project, although fortunately before this commercial real estate / economic crisis.

The menu is a combo of diner staples, waffle house, and some soul food and local stuff thrown in to boot. The BBQ burger with slaw on it was good, too bad I became a vegetarian! My only complaints are the lack of vegetarian items (although diners and breakfast type places are never really that tough for us) and lack of late hours.

text: Let me me re-cap my experience at Spa East. So i am newer to Philly and ever since I have been here I have been looking for a good place to get my eyebrows waxed. After about 5 minutes on hold, I was hung up on. This should have been my first clue as to how unorganized and unprofessional their employees are. I called back and someone new answered and said it would be no problem, I even made sure to ask that someone qualified would be waxing me and they insisted yes. Upon arriving i was greeted by the receptionist, her 3-daughters bickering, and my esthetician. 15 minutes later she brings me to the back where I assume she is taking me to lay down in a bed. Nope. Ok, so we get started...I tell her to "clean it up" well 10 minutes in she is still working on one eyebrow. She has now applied and re applied wax to the same locations multiple times. I almost missed my flight because I had no idea what was holding up the line and I sure wasn't moving. Granted, no airport is fun, but this one ranks up there with Chicago Ohare in my book!

text: Way overpriced and very unreliable. I want to give it bonus stars because its buses are pretty clean, but the horrible experiences I had during my four days in Philly cancel out any clean-bus sympathy stars. There's no reason to pay that much money to ride a bus in Philadelphia. And if you're going to pay that much money, the bus should probably come sometime. San Francisco's Muni has its own problems, but SEPTA makes Muni look like a world-class transit agency.
label: NEG

text: Having lived in Paris for several years, I've been yearning for that "je ne sais quoi" of a real Parisian brasserie.....and I'm glad that Parc finally brought it to Philly. I went to the Bastille Day opening night with my husband and 2 friends. When we arrived, the place was packed and we were told to wait a few minutes before being seated. Pessimistic as I am, I was sure that this was the beginning of a bad night....but it turned out to be just the opposite....we were seated in 10-15 minutes. Once at our table (love the open windows on Rittenhouse Park), everything on the menu sounded good. I picked a very traditional and delicious country pate appetizer and steak-frite entree. (God bless a Chef that can make a perfect Medium-Rare steak!) Our table also ordered a (few) carafes of red wine which were surprisingly good for a reasonable price. My only disappointment of the night was an undercooked creme brulee...but I'll go back to try again when its not the end of opening night! Overall the food was great, the atmosphere was authentic, and our service was perfect (not too fast - but I don't like that anyway...and not too slow - so that I considered eating my arm). I'll definitely be a frequent customer here!

text: I've never had a dog walker for my black lab Bella, and now I can't believe I had not started sooner. Think about it, people. And be realistic. And if you're lucky, you would get to play a little fetch after your owner gets home from a long day of work. If you're in Seattle, 9 months out of the year it's dark before your owner goes to work, and dark by the time they get back home. I am so grateful I found Teri, but my Bella is missing her walks and hikes dearly. text: Good, not great. If you are looking for Thai food, you won't regret going to this place. Granted, it is not as good or as fancy as Jasmine, but it is more than acceptable. text: I went to Bridgid's for the second time tonight, and I had a really enjoyable experience. I'm not sure it quite makes five stars in reality, but since I can't give it four-and-a-half, I'll give it five because I'm still full and satisfied from my 7:30 dinner. Although I felt that their beer selection was better last time (three words: Founder's Breakfast Stout), they DID have the Dogfish Head Palto Santo Marron, which I rarely see on tap anywhere, so that was a pleasant surprise. The other minor bother was that there was a terrible draft in the dining room, and it was a chilly night. They did compensate for this by lighting a nice, toasty fire, though, which made me happy. Now that the negatives are out of the way, I will move on to the good. Our server, Chris (the same server I had last time), was very pleasant and attentive. He promptly approached us after we were seated to take our drink and appetizer order. We ordered the Mozzarella and Roasted Red Pepper Salad and my roommate ordered the Brisket Chili, which came with cornbread. She loved it, and I thought the salad embodied perfection. There was a lot of fresh mozzarella, REAL greens (i.e., NOT iceberg), delicious roasted red peppers, and a mouthwatering balsamic vinaigrette. Their dressing was perfect in every sense of the word. I don't usually like creamier vinaigrettes, but this one was delicious. I've been trying to eat healthier lately, but tonight I decided to forget about that and order the Honey Fried Chicken. I am pretty glad I did. It was very tasty, without being too salty like some fried chicken, and not too greasy. The honey was a nice touch, but I think it could have used a tad bit less. They gave you a wing, a leg, and a breast, so it was a big portion, along with mashed potatoes (delicious, and presented beautifully!), a side salad (again, real greens!), and mixed green beans and carrots (not canned! Hallelujah!). I don't think I've ever touched a side of green beans at a restaurant, since they're usually canned, but these were garlicky and delicious. Since I'd already completely ruined myself with the fried chicken, I decided, why not get dessert too? Then you can roll yourself all the way home! I asked Chris what dessert he recommended, and he said to go with the Chocolate Mousse Pie. I'm usually not a pie person, but you can't really go wrong with chocolate mousse. So I got it, and definitely was not disappointed. It was creamy, rich, and had substance, unlike lots of these impostor mousses you see around. I finished with a cup of coffee and a Young's Chocolate Stout. Dessert doesn't get much better than that. What was even better than dessert, though, was the 15% off coupon we got in the weekly Money Mailer... the first time I've actually gotten use of that usual waste of paper! Overall, a great experience.

text: This place is fantastic! There is usually a long wait to get in but it's well worth the wait. It's BYOB so make sure to bring a good wine to go with your meal. The wait stuff and host are the same every time we go there which is nice because it gives you that "home town" feeling. The restaurant is small, but cozy. The food... The garlic knots are covered with olive oil, Parmesan, and of course tons of fresh garlic. They come straight from the oven so they are piping hot and usually don't last too long. They're also free with any entree. Lunch specials are offered and include a wide selection of smaller pasta dishes and very reasonably priced half sandwiches. Garlic knots are available with lunch, too. (can you tell how delicious they are?) Daily dinner specials are available and they are usually very tasty. My favorite entree is Chicken Siciliano. Chicken covered with eggplant, prosciutto, two cheeses, and wine sauce. This basically melts in your mouth. Jeff usually gets ones of the specials; the wild mushroom risotto with steak was one of the best. We've never ordered dessert there since we're usually so stuffed or we just go to Zwahlen's for dessert.
label: POS

text: This is my new favorite sushi place in the city. Yes, it's a bit pricey, but the amount and exceptional quality of the food makes it a great value. I had the Eternal Sunshine and it was scrumptious!

text: When going to a pet store, aside from pet food and supplies, you are probably seeking animals. Preferably, those animals would be alive. Hmmm, not here. When I first moved to the area I was excited to find a pet store right around the corner. However, when touring the store for the first time I stumbled upon fish that were belly up in several tanks. Although disturbing for a pet store, I tried to be optimistic. Other parts of the store were relatively clean. That's when I came across the parakeets. While 30 parakeets were happily wandering around a floor display, another 3 were pecking and stepping on an expired bird in the corner. Pretty gross. On a positive note, for a smaller store it has a good variety of pet food and supplies. However, if you love animals and want the people who sell you your pet supplies to care about animals as much as you do you might want to look elsewhere...
label: NEG

text: I'm writing this review in hopes to better humanity, even if it's in the smallest way. I was wondering why my seemingly perfect first floor, parkay wood, bi-level, Society Hill apartment was only $800 dollars a month. It had so much "character". Well, since move-in my kitchen has STUNK of gasoline. Since September there's been a hole in my floor. That's right, a hole. From plainly sitting in a chair, the leg just punctured through. Now, just to clarify, I am by no means obese nor does my chair have spikes for legs. Since November my "Leave it to Beaver" limited edition oven has been out of service. Every time I try to vacuum the BATHROOM CARPETING it comes off of the floor. My windows aren't sealed inviting about 500 new roommates a day who enjoy adding cobwebs and carcasses to my decor. The garbage disposal has been broken for about a month, so subsequently my apartment smells like I have a dead person in my closet. They've also come into my apartment without notifying me, which is extremely illegal. text: I wanted this place to be good. I really really wanted this place to be good. I was so disappointed it wasn't. You walk in, and the food selection area is right by the door, and the Ban Chan looks good. There is also a wide selection of it, which is great. Next to the self serve dishes, is self serve soju jan's. (shot glasses for soju for you non-koreans). The service was great and really attentive. It was really great. An excellent example of Korean hospitality, let's say unlike a certain Korean restuarant in Center City Philadelphia. Two problems. the grill temperature does not allow for proper cooking of Kalbi. second problem. The seasoning of the Kalbi and Bul gogi were terrible. The quality of the kalbi meat was really sub par. I went with a group of 8 friends. 4 never had Korean before. they really liked the food. The other 4, including my no Korean Wife, agreed it was possibly some of the poorest Kalbi and Bulgogi they ever had. I only went there because it was a BBQ buffet. If you are going to run a BBQ buffet, you have to improve the quality of the Kalbi and Bul Gogi. The Kim Chi was sub par at best. Kim chi is not that hard. you let it sit for three or four days to ferment, and it is perfect. I can't believe the food was bad and I am hoping it was a bad night because they were just so damn nice there. Please get better. Please. You were all so nice there I want to give you business. Especially because you are so close to University City, Right now, instead of 15 minutes away, we are still going to drive 45 minutes to go to Young Bin Kwan. My wife and I will probably go back in a few months to see if it got better. If you are Korean or a Korean BBQ afficianado, wait a bit. If you haven't had Korean, you'll probably think it's good, as my 4 first timer friends did. It's not terrible. Just not well seasoned meat. Did I mention they were SOOO Nice there though?

text: my boyfriend and i were looking for a "cultural place" to eat. he had mentioned moroccan. i was a little eeehhhh on the mention of it. let's be real. i love american foods. anyway, he had said i would probably like it. we had searched and found marrakesh on here. i didn't read much of the reviews to be honest i was just like eh, ok, let's go there and grub. we had trouble finding the place. it's smudged between south street and some alley. i wasn't sure if the building was it. i even forget if their was signage....but it kind of adds to the overall mood of the restaurant. (ps...i saw some drunk guy pissing on their wall....) we rang the doorbell only to have a tall, dark and well....not so handsome..but friendly gentlemen who sat us down. we were seated on a comfy morrocan-ish style couch filled with lush cushions and pillows. dimly lit living room or parlor to say it better. a little cramped and not as private but comfy indeed. the waiters were dressed in typical moroccan clothes....and i believe they may have been moroccan. ...so the food was a 7 course moroccan dream. it's basically a set menu but you do get to choose 2 items or so. i don't recommend getting the lamb. it tasted waaaayy to gamey for me. they have this delish eggy/almond/pastry pie course in the middle of all 7 courses. it almost looked/tasted like a funnel cake. i don't wanna spoil all the surprises they have to offer. but you really should check it out. probably not a first date choice. all in all, i'm now a fan off moroccan. thanks marrakesh! see you soon:)

text: Came by after the gym for a quick lunch with fam from out of town. We were seated quickly by the host. We had 2 servers trying to take our order. We ordered, me the baked chicken with 2 sides. So I called one of my 2 servers back to have them replaced, by something else, that was hot. The place is so cold that you can see the steam come off the plates while they are sitting on the line waiting to be delivered to your table. If they sit there for any period of time (like ours were), the air-conditioner will quickly chill your hot food. So the big deal really is the temperature of the food. Service, well these kids wouldn't do well anywhere else, without formal and proper training, but that OK, that is why this place is here, to help them acquire job skills. Just brought another for lunch and I'm disappointed as it tastes more like I'd originally expected, still a nicesize, just finished a little more than half but the beans I had the first day are missing, tons of lettuce and tomato this time around and onion which wasn't on there the 1st time, rice tastes like it could be day old or undercook not sure which. text: Overextended and unprofitable; it's like having our very own airline. We had a business account for several years. It was nice and convenient and affordable. Slowly, service declined and the costs shot up dramatically. In terms of accounting, it drove us crazy because PCS insisted on burying their invoices for the longest time in the bowels of their website, and whenever they hiked costs, they added or marginally increased add-on charges instead of the base cost per hour, which was unnecessarily deceptive. We began to assume that any trip, no matter how short, would cost no less than $15. We loved this service, but we can't afford to sympathize with their self-inflicted expansion problems just because they're a local nonprofit with a cute website. At this point, every other form of transportation, including taxis and owning a car, has proven cheaper than our PCS bill since we stopped using the PCS a few months ago.

text: I was asked to join my bff, her mom and her mom's friend for lunch in Doylestown and didn't ask where, was not told until we all met up in D'town. I was a bit disappointed, as there are other great choices, like Ooka, but I think the older women were not Sushi fans. Anyway, it was my friend's treat, so I went with the flow. First of all, the back bar area was just TOO dark. This was the middle of the afternoon and we could barely see the menu in the light. I actually like the atmosphere...and the gas fireplace gave off a nice warmth...I just think that for daytime...brighten it up a tad. Since I was not that thrilled with my sushi choice from the previous visit, I thought I'd play it relatively safe. The Roasted Beet Salad with Goat Cheese Fritter sounded great. It was okay. The goat cheese fritter was not hot, as you would expect a fried fritter to be, and the goat cheese inside was sort of gritty...not smooth and creamy, nothing special. The roasted beets/walnuts/field greens/dressing were okay, but again, I would have liked better lighting so I could tell what I was eating. So my safe choice for an entree was a hamburger...medium, with fries. Utterly unremarkable. For $12, I expect high quality beef, and this was ummm NOT. The burger had no flavor whatsoever, was cooked properly only on one half and was grissly. Though my guests and I didn't really discuss the food much (a hint that there wasn't much to discuss), I didn't hear any oohs and ahhs from anyone. We ate, we talked, we left.
label: NEG

text: Sook Hee's is my go-to business in the Comcast Center Market. Whenever I have an urge to get a piece of pizza, I force myself to go there instead. Then I walk around aimlessly, filling a basket with everything that looks delicious. The produce is fresh and priced well, and I like that everyone always says hello to me and is usually smiling. They have prepared fresh salads, sandwiches and the like at fair prices. I can usually buy ingredients to prepare salad for a week, though sometimes after a few days the spring mix gets slimy, it's a good alternative to buying a $10 lunch every day. Besides the produce, the smoothies, though a bit expensive to get every day, are a really refreshing occasional treat. In the display case are always the biggest carrots I have ever seen in my life. Sook Hee's is completely family run, so it kinda warms my heart when the cashier says "Dad?" It reminds me of my parents and always makes me smile.
label: POS

This venue is spacier than the center city tria, and doesn't feel as cramped. The cheese and meat platters are amazing, I never had a glass of wine there I didn't love, and all the servers are never short of amazing. Great ambiance, wine, service - all around phenominal! I highly recommend.

The oysters were the freshest I have had, and the Goat cheese dip was so good I was angry that I had to share it :) We all ordered Eggs benedict for our main course, and if I hadn't wanted the homemade mint chocolate chip ice cream sandwich so badly, I would have ordered a second Eggs Benny. Favorite drinks... Mary Pickford or the Dark and Stormy. Really good wine list as well. Red and white Bordeaux by the glass. I can't wait to go back. I am thinking of moving to Queen Village just to be closer!
